LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Here's how to watch, what to know, and an expert prediction before the Pats and Bears face off in Chicago Getty Images In the Week 7 edition of "Thursday Night Football," the Chicago Bears play host to the New England Patriots . Chicago is coming off a win in Caleb Williams ' return to the lineup, having held on for a 31-23 victory in a game that moved the Bears to 4-2 on the season. The Bears bounced back from their dispiriting loss to the division rival Green Bay Packers the week before, when the offense looked like a disaster with backup Tyson Bagent under center. Chicago will look to keep the good times rolling here. New England also won what -- on the surface -- looked like a close game against the New York Jets , but finished with a seven-point margin of victory thanks only to a late field goal. The Patriots have won three consecutive games after starting the season 1-2, and their quarterback has found a groove after looking nearly broken to start the year. The Pats, too, are looking to keep the train on the tracks on Thursday night. Will the Bears capture another win, or will the Patriots continue their hot streak? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game. Where to watch Bears vs. Patriots live Date: Thursday, Oct. 22 | Time: 8:20 p.m. ET Location: Soldier Field (Chicago) Streaming: Amazon Prime Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Bears -3, O/U 50.5 via DraftKings Sportsbook When the Patriots have the ball Drake Maye has found himself over the last three weeks, completing 66 of 103 passes for 878 yards, 10 touchdowns, and one interception after going just 51-of-80 for 585 yards, one touchdown, and six picks through the first three games of the season. Maye has rediscovered the deep ball, in particular, going 12 of 20 for 350 yards and four scores on throws beyond 15 yards in the last three games, per Tru Media. Before that, he was just 9 of 20 for 281 yards and four interceptions on those throws. Maye finished with a strong game against the Jets despite A.J. Brown looking horrifyingly bad in his return from an ankle injury. Brown dropped (at least) three passes and turned his 10 targets into only 27 yards. Maye also lost Romeo Doubs to a shoulder injury on an early-game touchdown pass, so he was working with a limited receiving corps behind Brown. Still, he threw for 235 yards and three touchdowns without turning the ball over. Brown will presumably be better here, and Chicago hasn't been great against outside receivers, but last week's return of Kyler Gordon could lead to slot man Demario Douglas having a tougher go of things than he has over the last few weeks. Kyle Williams could get in on the action with Doubs sidelined, though Efton Chism has been getting more snaps because the Patriots trust him as a blocker. Chicago checks in a surprising eighth in opponents' EPA per dropback so far this season, per Tru Media, thanks to a high sack rate and a few timely interceptions. Opponents have averaged 8.4 yards per attempt against the Bears, though, indicating that you can indeed move the ball through the air if you can get a pass off and avoid a turnover. Defensive coordinator Dennis Allen has generated pressure at an above-average rate (39.7% of dropbacks) despite working with a somewhat limited group up front, and the Patriots will be without two starting guards here. So, the running backs (particularly Rhamondre Stevenson ) will have to be on their game in pass protection on Thursday night. The Patriots have struggled to run the ball thus far this season, with Stevenson, TreVeyon Henderson and Corey Kiner combining for an average of just 3.9 yards per carry on 151 rushing attempts. Stevenson leads the way in the backfield largely because the Patriots trust him the most in short yardage and pass protection, but he hasn't been efficient or explosive. Henderson had an explosive rushing touchdown on his first run of the season but has failed to record one since. Kiner was a little-used third-stringer until he salted away the game against the Jets last Sunday. He could perhaps work his way into more touches after a nice showing in that game, given the rushing struggles of the two leads and the fact that Henderson also fumbled against New York. The Bears have allowed opponents 4.4 yards per carry on running-back rushes so far this season, with much of the success coming by way of yards before contact. It may be difficult for the Patriots to generate those types of yards with their injury issues along the offensive line, and their backs haven't exactly done the best job of breaking tackles this year, so the challenge of moving the offense down the field will likely fall squarely on Maye's right shoulder. When the Bears have the ball Caleb Williams returned last week from a three-game absence due to a hamstring injury and looked no worse for wear. Williams completed 30 of 36 passes for 305 yards and a touchdown. The Bears kept things simple for him with a 3.9-yard average depth of throw (eighth-lowest for any quarterback in a single game this season), per Tru Media, and he was extremely efficient as a result. Williams has only played in three games so far this year, but he's leading the league with a 72.5% completion rate and is up to a career-best 7.8 yards per attempt. And that's despite a truly awful game against the Vikings in Week 2, where he went 15-of-26 for just 138 yards and an interception. In his first couple of appearances, it seemed like journeyman wideout Kalif Raymond (14 targets in Weeks 1 and 2) was his primary option, but on Sunday, it was Luther Burden III and Colston Loveland -- the most expected options -- leading the way with eight and seven targets, respectively. Rome Odunze saw five looks. Given the way they're each deployed, it seems likely that Odunze will see a bunch of Christian Gonzalez 's coverage on Thursday night -- especially with Carlton Davis III ruled out. Odunze is the biggest of the trio and plays most often on the perimeter, and he also tends to run the most routes. If that's the way things go, we should expect the passing game to flow through Burden and Loveland yet again. The Patriots have allowed opponents to complete 31 of 46 passes for 301 yards on throws to the slot this season, per Tru Media. Burden could have a nice night working inside if he's on the field more often than he was last week (eight targets on only 18 routes), though Marcus Jones does have an interception this season and is allowing only 1.46 yards per coverage snap in the slot, per Pro Football Focus. By contrast, New England has allowed only 29 catches for 279 yards to tight ends to date, so Loveland may not find the coverage as friendly. The Bears would do well to line him up all over the formation rather than solely in line, and perhaps use multi-tight end sets where he plays more of a receiver role, and Cole Kmet or Sam Roush handles the blocking aspects of the position. The Bears also tried against Atlanta to do what they do best: run the ball with volume. D'Andre Swift and Roschon Johnson (the latter filling in for the injured Kyle Monangai ) combined for 29 carries. They ran for only 96 yards on those totes, but they did find the end zone three times. Chicago's offensive line actually created some nice push, generating 1.45 yards before contact per carry, according to Tru Media, but the backs slumped to only 1.83 yards after contact, as they combined for only four broken tackles. (For context, consider that the Seahawks ' running backs combined for 10 in their awful game against the Broncos on Thursday night.) The Pats have allowed only 3.9 yards per rush this season, thanks in part to yielding an average of only 0.75 yards before contact. Swift and Johnson (Monangai is out again) will have to do a better job of breaking tackles this time around if they want to generate yardage and create favorable down-and-distance scenarios for Williams and the passing game. I see this being a high-scoring game, what with two offenses that can pile up points quickly. Chicago's offense in two non-rain/non-Brian Flores games with Caleb Williams under center has been electric, particularly on the ground, and Caleb Williams opens things up for the passing game. New England is struggling to run the ball, but Drake Maye has been on fire as of late. I'll lean toward the Bears here because of the Patriots' injury issues along the offensive line, which could hold the run game back further and put even more on Maye's shoulders. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict this weekend's top games Getty Images What did we learn in Week 6? The Houston Texans are officially back, as is Caleb Williams with the Chicago Bears , and we have some serious questions about the Los Angeles Rams , who were upset by the Arizona Cardinals at home last Sunday. The Cardinals now have more wins at SoFi Stadium this year than the Rams and Los Angeles Chargers combined. This week, the Pittsburgh Steelers and New Orleans Saints will play the first-ever NFL game in Paris, the San Francisco 49ers look to remain perfect against the Atlanta Falcons , and Kenneth Walker III aims to lead the Kansas City Chiefs to victory over his former team, the Seattle Seahawks . This could be a revenge game for the ages. Which teams should you pick in Week 7, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Oct. 21 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. New England Patriots at Chicago Bears (-3) (TNF) Dajani (Bears -3): I can't remember the last time I've been this excited for a Thursday night game. Caleb Williams will suit up for the first time at home since his hamstring injury, and this is the first Bears home game since the passing of Mike Ditka. I have concerns about this Bears pass defense and how it will fare against a red-hot Drake Maye , but the fact is that Chicago has allowed 9.3 points per game at home this season. The Bears' offense has also averaged 35 points per game in their four wins, and I think Williams is out to make a statement. This will be a high-flying affair that comes down to the very end, and a push is very much in play. But give me Chicago at home, with the backing of an emotionally charged atmosphere. Remember, the Bears' lone Super Bowl win came against the New England Patriots under Ditka. … Prediction: Bears 28, Patriots 24 Dubin (Bears -3): I also see this being a high-scoring game, with two offenses that can pile up points quickly. Chicago's offense in two non-rain/non-Brian Flores games with Caleb Williams under center has been electric, particularly on the ground, and Caleb Williams opens things up for the passing game. New England is struggling to run the ball, but Drake Maye has been on fire as of late. I'll lean toward the Bears here because of the Patriots' injury issues along the offensive line, which could hold the run game back further and put even more on Maye's shoulders. … Prediction: Bears 31, Patriots 27 Pittsburgh Steelers (-3.5) vs. New Orleans Saints (Paris) Dajani (Saints +3.5): The Steelers are impossible to figure out. From week-to-week — or even half-to-half, as evidenced by last week's overtime victory against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . If you're going to give me the hook at +3.5 in an international game, I'm probably going to take it. The Saints are a perfect 8-0 ATS in their last eight games away from home, and are 3-0 ATS all-time in international games. I think Gayle Benson's recent comments stirred up the locker room, and the Saints responded with a win in which they dropped 34 points — even if it came against the New York Giants . … Prediction: Steelers 23, Saints 20 Dubin (Steelers -3.5): The Saints finally played a game from ahead last week against the Giants, and they didn't necessarily look comfortable doing it. They have mostly been a second-half offensive team throughout this season, struggling early on before piling up yards and points in comeback mode. The New England Patriots and Drake Maye are riding a three-game winning streak into their primetime matchup with the Chicago Bears and former No. 1 overall pick Caleb Williams on Thursday Night Football. Williams is making his second straight start after he missed three games earlier this season with a hamstring injury. The star quarterback showed no signs of rust in Week 6, completing 30 of his 36 pass attempts in a win over the Atlanta Falcons, improving the Bears to 4-2 this season. Chicago is favored in this matchup, and it needs every win it can get with the NFC North sporting four teams over .500 through the first six weeks. The Bears may be getting a little extra love in this matchup because of all the injuries for the Patriots, who have been decimated at receiver (Mack Hollins and Romeo Doubs on IR) and on their offensive line. Still, New England has won three games in a row, and Maye is back in the MVP conversation with 10 touchdown passes during that streak. He has a tough matchup ahead against a Chicago team that is in the top 10 in the league in EPA/Play and success rate on defense this season. So, how should bettors attack Thursday’s showdown? In the leadup to this marquee matchup, the SI Betting team has made a bunch of game picks, prop bet selections and more. I’ve decided to share some of our favorites all in one place to help bettors get the most of this primetime matchup between two playoff contenders in Week 7. He’s taking the UNDER even with two star quarterbacks facing off: Unless I'm missing something, I'm not quite sure why the total for this game is in the 50s. Sure, the Bears' offense is much more explosive with Caleb Williams at quarterback, but even with that being the case, these two offenses rank 12th and 14th in EPA per play this season and seventh and 12th in success rate. A high total would make sense if the two defenses in this game were bad, but they rank in the top half of the league in most metrics. In fact, the Bears' defense comes into this game ranking fourth in opponent success rate. The Patriots' offense is also dealing with some injuries. A.J. Brown is questionable, and Romeo Doubs is on IR. Their run game can't be relied on to help out the injuries at wide receiver, as it's been largely ineffective all season. I'll bet the UNDER on Thursday Night Football for the second straight week. Maye started the season in an awful slump, throwing just one score and six picks in his first three games. Since then, he’s flipped the script, tossing 10 scores (at least three in each game) over the last three weeks, leading New England to wins over Buffalo, Las Vegas and the New York Jets. Maye is right back in the mix to win the MVP, and I like this matchup against a Chicago defense that has allowed nine passing scores in 2026 and was torched by Bryce Young and Jordan Love already this season. The Bears have benefitted from some soft scheduling in terms of the quarterbacks they’ve faced, but Love threw for 367 yards against them in Week 5, and Chicago has allowed the 15th-most passing yards in the league. New England loves to throw the ball, and I think the odds for this prop are pretty favorable considering the fact that Maye threw 31 touchdown passes in 2025. Last season, the young tight end really came on in the second half, finishing the campaign with six touchdown receptions. He’s only picked up one in 2026, and New England has allowed just one receiving score to the position this season. Still, Loveland’s role is growing with 21 targets over the last three games. He’s a solid bet at this price after his best game of the season. D’Andre Swift has a ton of carries for the Bears this season, handling 94 touches for 398 yards and six scores on the ground, but he hasn’t been super efficient since Week 1. Swift ran for 124 yards on 18 carries against Carolina in the season opener, yet he has just one other game (Week 3 against Philadelphia) where he’s picked up over 60 rushing yards. Backup Kyle Monangai (turf toe) has been banged up, but Swift still split time with Roschon Johnson in Week 6 and has played just 56.7 percent of the Bears’ snaps this season. New England is allowing just 3.9 yards per carry in the 2026 campaign, and I wouldn’t be shocked if Swift came up short of this rushing total again on Thursday. He has averaged less than four yards per carry in two of the last three weeks, putting up 58, 43 and 44 rushing yards during that stretch. away.headline: Cole Kmet suffered ‘likely season-ending injury' during Bears-Patriots game: Reports
away.blurb: Chicago Bears’ star tight end Cole Kmet is believed to have suffered a serious and potentially season-ending knee injury on a fourth-quarter reception against the New England Patriots Thursday night at Soldier Field, according to reports. NFL Network and ESPN reporter Ian Rapoport said Kmet was undergoing testing Friday morning. “Until those results come back, there is no finality,” Rapoport wrote in a post on X. Kmet had caught a pass on second down from quarterback Caleb Williams with 5:34 left to go in the game, and was moving toward the first-down marker when he was hit by two Patriots defenders. Kmet immediately began grabbing his right knee on the sideline, and was tended to by trainers for the Bears. After the TV timeout, Kmet was seen being carted off the field, giving a thumbs up to Bears fans as he left the field. The game ended in a 30-24 Bears victory . When asked at Kmet’s injury status following the game, Coach Ben Johnson didn’t sound optimistic. “We’ll know more tomorrow, but I don’t think it looked very good,” he said. Kmet has been a key reserve player for the Bears this season, serving as a mentor to Colston Loveland and still playing significant snaps for Chicago during the season. If Kmet misses any time, rookie Sam Roush would likely see more action on offense. Johnson was expected to address the media at 1 p.m. Friday. home.headline: What we learned about Caleb Williams and Chicago Bears in NFL Week 6
home.source: USA TODAY College Sports Wire on MSN
home.blurb: The Chicago Bears were ignited by the return of former USC Trojan Caleb Williams and teammate Kyler Gordon. Both players did not miss a beat and put together dominant performances. As a result, the Bears ' offense and defense both looked good enough to make a run at the Super Bowl. Coltson Loveland was disappointing at the start of the season. Last week, however, the return of starting quarterback Caleb Williams helped him get his confidence back. Loveland had a spectacular touchdown catch on the opening drive, and he finished with 6 catches for 65 yards. The Bears offense is at its best when Loveland is making plays. It looks like the Bears' biggest playmaker is back. The NFC conference is wide open and up for grabs. The San Francisco 49ers and the Minnesota Vikings are both undefeated, but both teams have weaknesses the Bears can exploit. When this Bears team is healthy and with the return of Kyle Monangai on offense, the Bears can beat anyone in the league. Here is what we learned about the Bears in NFL Week 6: Caleb Williams looks like a top 5 quarterback One of the biggest weaknesses of Caleb Williams' game is his accuracy and his ability to play on time. Against the Atlanta Falcons, those weaknesses looked like strengths. Caleb started the game off 24/24, not missing a beat. He finished the game with an 83.3% completion percentage. That proves Caleb Williams is one of the best quarterbacks in the league. Right now, he leads the NFL with a 72.5% completion percentage. His development in year 3 has been exciting to watch and scary for the rest of the NFL to see. Kyle Monangai is such a pivotal piece to the offense Without Kyle Monangai, the Bears' run game has taken a big hit. He is the physical back that this offense needs. Without him, D'Andre Swift is a lot easier to limit. In his last game, Monangai had 30 carries for 146 yards and a touchdown. Through just 4 games, he has 324 yards and 3 touchdowns. In his absence, his true value to the offense has been on full display. It was too early to close the door on Colston Loveland When healthy Kyler Gordon is one of the best at his position in the NFL In only 16 snaps, Kyler Gordon showed he can make a massive impact. He tallied 3 sacks and a tackle for a loss on his first snap of the season. Dennis Allen is able to get extremely creative when Kyler Gordon is on the field. Gordon could be the key to the Bears' defense going from good to great. Bears are 2nd-best team in the NFC when healthy Contact/Follow @TrojansWire on X (formerly Twitter) and like our page on Facebook to follow ongoing coverage of USC Trojans news, notes and opinion. Pittsburgh has playoff expectations in the 2026 season, and new head coach Mike McCarthy has his team at a 4-2 start through six weeks. However, the AFC North has four teams over .500, putting the Steelers in a spot where they can't afford many losses early in the season. Meanwhile, New Orleans is off to a 2-4 start, snapping a three-game skid in Week 6 when they beat the New York Giants. Shough and company have performed pretty well on offense, but New Orleans is sitting in third place in the division at just 2-4 through the first six weeks. This is technically a home game for the Saints, and they're set as underdogs against Rodgers and the Steelers. This line opened up 2.5 points (Pittsburgh favored), and it has since moved to three. The Steelers have a top-10 defense in EPA/Play, while the Saints are a bottom-10 unit and sit dead last in the league in EPA/Rush. That could offer some interesting prop spots with the Steelers' backfield of Rico Dowdle and Jaylen Warren looking pretty strong in their Week 6 win against Tampa Bay. So, how should bettors wager on the NFL’s first-ever game in France? All week long, the SI Betting team has made game picks, player prop selections and a few anytime touchdown scorer choices for this game in Paris. So, why not put all of our favorites in one spot? This column is a one-stop shop for the NFL Paris matchup to get bettors ready for the first game in Sunday’s 12-game slate. Best NFL Picks and Predictions for Steelers vs. Saints Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook Pittsburgh Steelers -3 (-110) vs. New Orleans Saints – Iain MacMillan Chris Olave Anytime TD (+185) – Peter Dewey Jaylen Warren OVER 63.5 Rushing Yards (-114) – Peter Dewey Germie Bernard 5+ Receptions (-167) – Peter Dewey Every week, SI Betting’s Iain MacMillan shares his favorite bet for each NFL game in his Road to 272 column . He’s backing Pittsburgh to cover the spread in Paris as a “road” favorite: The Steelers' run game against the Saints' run defense will be the biggest difference-maker in this game. Pittsburgh has done a great job running the football this season, ranking fifth in rush EPA, and Jaylen Warren is averaging 5.5 yards per carry. Now they face a Saints defense that's last in both opponent rush EPA and opponent rush success rate, while also giving up 4.8 yards per rush. If Warren can be effective on the ground, the Saints' offense will struggle to keep pace. The Steelers' defense is top 10 in the NFL in both opponent EPA per play and opponent success rate. Let's hope that defense travels. I'm going to back the Steelers as favorites in France. Saints wide receiver Chris Olave has two touchdowns in the 2026 season, and he’s actually seen his targets drop (13 total in the last two weeks) after four straight double-digit target games to open the season. Despite that, I’m buying low on the former Ohio State star on Sunday. The Steelers have allowed just six passing scores this season and are sixth in the league in EPA/Pass, but Olave has been the focal point of this Saints team that throws the ball almost as much as anyone in the NFL. The Saints are third in the league in pass attempts in 2026, and Olave has drawn 61 looks in six games. There are other options to consider for the Saints (Devaughn Vele, Juwan Johnson), but I’ll gladly take a true No. 1 receiver at nearly 2/1 to find the end zone in Week 7. The Saints have been awful against the run this season, ranking dead last in the NFL in EPA/Rush and allowing 4.8 yards per carry. That’s a great sign for Pittsburgh running back Jaylen Warren, who is averaging 5.5 yards per carry and already has 460 rushing yards in six games this season. Even with Rico Dowdle (toe) returning to action in Week 6, Warren led the backfield by playing over 74 percent of the snaps and handling 14 carries. He finished the day with 50 rushing yards and 28 receiving yards. While this prop is a little higher than that, Warren had a three-game streak with 90 or more rushing yards snapped in Week 6. Tampa Bay is third in the NFL in EPA/Rush this season, so this is a much easier matchup for Warren in Week 7. He’s handled at least 10 carries in every game, including 14 or more in four straight. Since the veteran has taken the clear lead in this backfield, I expect him to be the biggest beneficiary against this Saints defense. Rookie receiver Germie Bernand has been forced into a bigger role with Pittsburgh's injuries this season, and he’s thriving in it. The second-round pick had nine targets and six catches in Week 5 against Indianapolis, and he followed that up with a massive day in the win against Tampa Bay. Bernard found the end zone for the first time in his career, and he caught 11 of his 12 looks from Rodgers for 87 yards. Since Rodgers isn’t really pushing the ball down the field, I love this receptions prop for Bernand, as he’s emerged as the No. 2 receiver behind DK Metcalf. The rookie played over 91 percent of the snaps in each of the last two weeks, and he’s clearly established a solid rapport with Rodgers. I think he’s a great target against a Saints defense that is in the bottom 10 in the league in EPA/Pass, opponent completions and opponent passing yards in 2026. The league heads to Paris for Week 7 of the 2026 season where Aaron Rodgers and the Pittsburgh Steelers are set to take on the New Orleans Saints and second-year signal-caller Tyler Shough. Pittsburgh is right back in the playoff mix in the AFC this season, sitting at 4-2 through six weeks after a comeback win against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 6. It hasn't always been pretty for the Steelers this season, but their defense (sixth in EPA/Play) has been one of the best in the league, helping them stay in games. Rodgers ranks just 30th amongst quarterbacks with at least 50 plays this season in success rate, which is a bit of a concern against a New Orleans team that has been able to put points on the board this season. The Saints’ defense is just 27th in EPA/Play, but Shough has moved the ball pretty well in his second NFL season, leading New Orleans to a win over the New York Giants last Sunday. Oddsmakers have set the Steelers as “road” favorites in this matchup, and they need every win they can get with the AFC North featuring four over .500 teams through the first six weeks. All season long, the SI Betting team has shared our final score predictions for every NFL game, and with the league exploring the Paris market, we’re still here to give picks. With Pittsburgh in the thick of a playoff race and New Orleans looking to get back in the NFC South mix, who wins in Paris? Pittsburgh has done a great job running the football this season, ranking fifth in rush EPA, and Jaylen Warren is averaging 5.5 yards per carry. Now they face a Saints defense that's last in both opponent rush EPA and opponent rush success rate, while also giving up 4.8 yards per rush. If Warren can be effective on the ground, the Saints' offense will struggle to keep pace. The Steelers' defense is top 10 in the NFL in both opponent EPA per play and opponent success rate. Let's hope that defense travels. I'm going to back the Steelers as favorites in France. I love MacMillan’s reasoning for this bet, and I’m also taking the Steelers to win on Sunday morning. Shough has put up some big passing stats in games this season, but he’s still just 20th in success rate amongst QBs with at least 50 plays in the 2026 campaign. This New Orleans team also has one good win (over Baltimore) and some questionable losses through six weeks. The defense is one of the worst in the NFL, and Week 6 showed that Pittsburgh’s defense can take over a game, especially against a young quarterback. The Steelers shut down Tampa Bay in the second half and ended up winning in overtime despite Rodgers and the offense struggling most of the day. I don’t expect a ton of points from Pittsburgh – that simply hasn’t been the team's M.O. in 2026 – but it should do enough to cover in Week 7. Riding a two-game win streak heading into Week 7, the Steelers still have things to clean up as they look to keep pace in the race for both the AFC North and one of three Wild Card spots in the conference. Regardless, Pittsburgh is 4-2 for a fourth-straight season and has what some may consider a must-win type of game vs. New Orleans given how tough its schedule gets immediately following its Week 9 bye. With that, here are three bold predictions for the Steelers as they look to take down the Saints. Oct 18, 2026; Tampa, Florida, USA; Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers (8) throws a pass during the third quarter against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Raymond James Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kim Klement Neitzel-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Steelers Put Up 400+ Yards of Offense Steelers Put Up 400+ Yards of Offense Pittsburgh's offense largely falls near the middle of the pack, averaging the 12th-fewest yards (320.5) and the 15th-fewest points (22.8) per game in the league. Those numbers are dragged down quite a bit by the team's poor outing against the New England Patriots in Week 2, however, during which they scored just three points with 235 yards of offense. Under Mike McCarthy, the Steelers have proven that they're at least capable of explosive offensive performances. For example, they scored 30 points with 411 yards in a Week 3 victory over the Cincinnati Bengals and put up 34 points in a Week 5 win over the Indianapolis Colts. It's possible that Pittsburgh comes out a bit sluggish against the Saints in Paris after arriving later in the week, but the formula is there for the black and gold to have another huge performance. New Orleans' defense is currently tied with the Arizona Cardinals for the most points allowed per game (29.7) while also giving up the fourth-most yards per contest (377.7). The Saints have struggled to consistently get after the quarterback too, as their 33.2 percent pressure rate (per SumerSports ) is the fourth-worst in the NFL despite having 15 sacks. The Steelers' offense already had their way with one of the worst defenses in the league in the Colts, and there's no reason they can't do the same vs. New Orleans by finishing with over 400 yards of total offense. Pittsburgh Forces Two Turnovers The Saints' offense cannot be taken lightly. Even though first-round wide receiver Jordyn Tyson has yet to play this season with a hamstring injury, while franchise left tackle Kelvin Banks Jr. has been out since Week 3 after undergoing ankle surgery, they are still averaging the 11th-most points (25.3) in the league. At the same time, quarterback Tyler Shough has thrown five interceptions and lost three fumbles while New Orleans as a whole has turned the ball over 12 times , which is tied for the third-most in the NFL. Pittsburgh, meanwhile, has 10 takeaways on the year, which is tied with five other teams for the second-most behind the Green Bay Packers and Seattle Seahawks at 11. The Steelers' defense is among the better units in the league, as they allow the sixth-lowest EPA per play (-0.1) and the seventh-fewest yards per game (307.5). New Orleans is capable of doing a little bit of damage, but Pittsburgh's defense has stepped up and largely made the necessary plays when it's needed to. Winning the turnover margin is always crucial, and considering how susceptible the Saints are to giving the ball away, the Steelers will end up with two takeaways in this one. Oct 18, 2026; Tampa, Florida, USA; Pittsburgh Steelers safety Jaquan Brisker (3) and Pittsburgh Steelers safety Robert Spears-Jennings (28) celebrate after a play during the fourth quarter against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Raymond James Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Morgan Tencza-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Steelers Win by Two Scores Steelers Win by Two Scores Pittsburgh is short-handed along the interior of its defensive line with Sebastian Joseph-Day (triceps) joining Derrick Harmon (foot) on the reserve/injured list. The same can be said at wide receiver, as Michael Pittman Jr. (foot) and Roman Wilson (finger) are on IR as well while Ben Skowronek (calf) will miss his second-straight game . Cornerback Brandin Echols (hamstring) will be sidelined too, and there are also some questions about Rico Dowdle's (knee) availability after he was deemed questionable to suit up on the Steelers' final injury report of the week. Still, this is a game the Steelers should win. Again, maybe they aren't at tip-top shape playing overseas, but they're simply the better and more talented team. The Saints are not a pushover by any means and have the potential to make things tough for Pittsburgh, as evidenced by their comeback win over the Baltimore Ravens on the road in Week 2. That being said, New Orleans is 2-4 for a reason. Its defense is among the worst in the league, and while its offense is a formidable unit, it's going to have a tough time keeping up with the Steelers. After notching their first two-score win of the season in Week 5 vs. Indianapolis, who profiles similarly to the Saints, Pittsburgh will do so once again in France and move to 5-2. However, the New Orleans Saints' defense does not inspire confidence in stopping the Pittsburgh Steelers. Aaron Rodgers remains a solid quarterback at age 42, passing for nearly 1,500 yards with 12 touchdowns and five interceptions. Allowing 377 passing yards to Jameis Winston and J.J. McCarthy does not bode well for New Orleans. While the win over the New York Giants was notable, New York lacked a running back like Jaylen Warren to keep the Saints' defense honest. away.headline: Steelers' TJ Watt pops up on injury report with new concern
away.blurb: The former Defensive Player of the Year didn’t practice on Wednesday for a rest designation. But, then he was limited in practice on Thursday because of a calf injury. This is a new injury to the public. There was some good defensive news coming out of the Steelers’ injury report, though. Cornerback Jalen Ramsey was limited on Thursday after not practicing the day prior with a wrist injury, so that was improvement. Outside linebacker Alex Highsmith was also limited with a groin issue, the same designation as Wednesday. Related Articles Giants DC Threatens Players Amid 'Unacceptable' Behavior, Calls Out 'Traitors' The Pittsburgh Steelers haven’t been able to catch a break from injuries the last few weeks. It seems like a new star player is being added to the injury report each week. Thursday’s injury report included a surprising name, one that Steelers fans wish wasn’t on the list: edge rusher T.J. Watt. It’s unclear when or how Watt suffered the calf injury. But, now there’s a possibility, even if just a slight one, that Watt could miss Sunday’s game in Paris against the New Orleans Saints . Watt being absent for a game is always a loss for the Steelers. He can always make big and important plays for his team. Through six games this season, Watt’s recorded 4.5 sacks (tied for eighth in the league), 15 tackles, one interception, one forced fumble and one fumble recovery. Veteran tackle Cameron Heyward didn’t practice Wednesday or Thursday for rest designations, but he should be good to go come Sunday. Safety DeShon Elliott recorded his second-straight full practice on Thursday, meaning he’ll likely play on Sunday. It would mark Elliott’s first game since last October after he suffered an MCL sprain, hyperextended knee and a hamstring injury. Pittsburgh Steelers veteran safety DeShon Elliott was trending in the right direction at practice throughout the week. The team took the last step for Elliott to make his 2026 season debut Sunday against the New Orleans Saints . On Saturday, the Steelers announced they have activated Elliott from the reserve/injured list. He will be eligible to play Sunday against the Saints in the NFL's first-ever regular season game in Paris, France. Elliott fully practiced Wednesday and Thursday before the team flew to Europe. The Steelers then canceled their Friday practice in France. The veteran safety doesn't have a designation on the team's injury report. Barring a last-minute setback, Elliott will dress for the first time this season versus the Saints. On Wednesday, the Steelers released safety Rayshawn Jenkins. The team didn't make a corresponding move, which left open a roster spot for Elliott on Saturday. Elliott started this season on the PUP list because of a knee injury he sustained last season. Elliott hyperextended his knee, which required surgery, in Week 8 almost exactly a year ago on October 26. Steelers Activate DeShon Elliott for Week 7 The Jenkins release was a pretty strong giveaway that Elliott would play in Week 7. In five games during 2025, Elliott posted 38 combined tackles. He also had one tackle for loss, three quarterback hits, one sack, two pass defenses and one interception. Elliott began his career in the AFC North with the Baltimore Ravens . He spent three seasons with the Ravens, where he became a regular starter in 2020. The 49ers hosted Trice for a visit after the Falcons released him on Tuesday, Oct. 20. The former third-round pick is looking for a new home after finally making his NFL regular-season debut in 2026, following two injury-plagued seasons in Atlanta. San Francisco's defensive staff includes former Falcons head coach Raheem Morris, now the 49ers' defensive coordinator. Although Morris coached Atlanta in 2024 and 2025, Trice never played under him in a regular-season game. Trice spent his first two NFL seasons sidelined by injuries while Morris led the Falcons. If Trice joins the 49ers, he would be the second former Falcon Morris has brought to San Francisco. The 49ers signed edge rusher Khalid Kareem from the Falcons' Practice Squad before the season opener. Atlanta selected Trice with the 74th overall pick in the third round of the 2024 NFL Draft out of Washington, hoping he could develop into a productive pass rusher. However, his professional career got off to a difficult start when he tore his ACL during his first preseason game as a rookie. Trice missed the entire 2024 season before suffering another setback with the same knee during the 2025 campaign. Those injuries kept him out of a regular-season game during his first two years with the organization. The 25-year-old entered training camp healthy in 2026 but did not make Atlanta's initial 53-man roster. After clearing waivers, he returned to the Falcons' practice squad in early September. Atlanta gave Trice three weeks of practice squad elevations to prove himself. His Week 3 performance against the Green Bay Packers stood out, as he recorded four quarterback hurries while helping Atlanta's defensive front generate pressure. The Falcons eventually signed Trice to their active roster on Oct. 17 after using all three of his standard practice squad elevations. However, his time back on the 53-man roster was brief, as Atlanta released him three days later after the Falcons signed Charles Snowden from the Washington Commanders Practice Squad . Trice appeared in four games for Atlanta this season, recording two total tackles and one pass defended, according to the Falcons' official release announcement and NFL statistics. He also showed flashes as a pass rusher, particularly with his four quarterback hurries against Green Bay. For San Francisco, the visit offers a chance to evaluate a young defender who has faced significant adversity but is finally getting meaningful NFL playing time. His experience working along the defensive front could give the 49ers another option as they assess their depth at linebacker and edge defender. Morris' presence adds an interesting connection between Trice's former team and his potential next destination, even without a previous on-field relationship between the two. Trice has yet to establish himself as a consistent NFL contributor, but his healthy return in 2026 gave him his first chance to show the ability that earned him a third-round selection. Whether that opportunity continues in San Francisco remains to be seen. picks.headline: NFL predictions: Can Falcons take advantage of 49ers injuries?
picks.blurb: NFL predictions: Can Falcons take advantage of 49ers injuries? - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football UCF stuns No. 2 BYU for its first-ever win over Top 5 team TRENDING College football updates Valkyries even WNBA Finals Kimi Antonelli on US GP pole NFL injury updates Brewers take Game 1 NFL predictions: Can Falcons take advantage of 49ers injuries? SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 19: Mac Jones #10 of the San Francisco 49ers is rushed by Zach Harrison #96 of the Atlanta Falcons during the third quarter in the game at Levi's Stadium on October 19, 2025 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Lachlan Cunningham/Getty Images) | Getty Images Kevin Knight Sat, October 24, 2026 at 1:17 AM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Atlanta Falcons are sitting at 2-4 after a disappointing two-week stretch. Atlanta desperately needed to find a win over the past few weeks, instead dropping a game to the Tyler Huntley-led Ravens and (understandably) to the finally healthy Bears. The Falcons didn't play terribly in either game, but in both, it was too little too late from Atlanta's offense. TNow the team enters the unenviable situation of needing a win against an undefeated 49ers team that has pretty consistently looked like one of the NFL's best units despite a growing injury list. That lengthy injury list, along with some rest and off-field advantages, could help the Falcons pull off the unlikely upset in Week 7. The bettors seem to think so as well, as Atlanta is just a 2.5-point home underdog according to FanDuel. Falcons vs 49ers predictions On paper, the 49ers are clearly the superior team. San Francisco is one of only a handful of teams who are top-10 in both offense and defense, and one of only two who are top-5 in both categories. To put it simply, there aren't any obvious glaring weaknesses on this team—except their long injury list, which is only growing heading into Week 7. That's something the Falcons will have to take advantage of to come away with an improbable victory. The 49ers offense struggled mightily once Mike Evans, who Falcons fans know quite well, left the game against the Commanders in Week 6. Washington was close to mounting a comeback, but was ultimately unsuccessful due to their own issues. Evans, along with Deebo Samuel, have both been declared out for Week 7. Those are major losses, and when combined with San Francisco's other injuries at the position, could be too much for the passing game to overcome. Atlanta is dealing with their own injury problems, particularly on defense. Starting slot corner Billy Bowman and linebacker Divine Deablo are both out, and three other cornerbacks are questionable. It does sound like A.J. Terrell and C.J. Henderson are likely to play on Sunday, but a new injury (and questionable designation) for rookie Avieon Terrell throw a wrench into things. Veteran Mike Hughes, who has struggled mightily this season, will be on track to start again unless those players are cleared. Already down Jalon Walker and James Pearce Jr., Atlanta is looking at questionable designations for Za'Darius Smith and Samson Ebukam on the edge. Standout interior pass rusher Gervon Dexter Sr. also picked up a questionable tag heading into the weekend. Atlanta is perilously thin on the edge and can't afford any more losses here. If Atlanta can get most of these players in the game on Sunday, they may have a significant health advantage over San Francisco. History is also unkind to West Coast teams traveling to play in the 1pm timeslot on the East Coast, and the 49ers are working off a rest disadvantage after just playing on Monday Night Football. Health and extra rest could be critical to the Falcons pulling off the upset. That'll, plus Atlanta figuring out how to deal with blitz pressure and opposing defenses crowding the line of scrimmage. Michael Penix Jr. has been outstanding when kept clean this season, but he's absolutely cratered when faced with pressure. Part of the issue is that Atlanta has been allowing the fastest time to pressure in the NFL by quite a wide margin, giving Penix little time to react. Hopefully that's been a major point of emphasis in practice this week. I'm not confident in Atlanta's ability to take down a superior opponent, especially coming off the past two weeks. So I'm going to say that the 49ers should win this game. However, Atlanta's potential health advantage along with the extra rest and the West Coast-East Coast factors could combine to give the Falcons a real shot in this one. Plus, Evan would be remiss if I didn't mention the RED HELMET ENERGY. It's uncanny, but the Falcons typically play great in this uniform. Will they pull it off? That's the question I don't feel confident answering.

away.headline: 49ers linked to Pro Bowl pass-rusher amid mounting injury issues
away.blurb: Bosa can return any week now, but the 49ers have been bracing to be without him for several weeks after he suffered a calf injury during warm-ups a few weeks ago. “Considering how important pressure is in the modern NFL, especially against the elite passers teams inevitably come up against in the playoffs, the Niners would be wise to bolster their edge-rushing unit with one of the best available free agents: Joey Bosa. The San Francisco 49ers may just be the best team in the NFL , but their mounting injury issues will catch up to them eventually. The team’s wide receiver corps has been ravaged in recent weeks with Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel, De’Zhaun Stribling, and Demarcus Robinson all going down with various ailments. The defensive side of the ball has also been hit hard by the injury bug as well. Defensive tackles Alfred Collins, CJ West, Sam Okuayinonu, edge-rushers Nick Bosa and Mikail Kamara, linebackers Nick Martin and Garret Wallow, cornerback Nate Hobbs, and safeties Marques Sigle and Darrick Forest are all either on injured reserve or have missed several weeks with their respective injuries. In the meantime, Bleacher Report’s Alex Kay believes San Francisco should add to its pass-rush pool by signing a five-time Pro Bowler who’s quite familiar with one of the team’s top players. “While San Francisco features a top-five defense, it hasn’t generated pressure on a consistent basis,” Kay wrote . “An extended absence from top edge-rusher Nick Bosa — who has been dealing with a calf injury since Week 2 — has hindered the team’s ability to get after opposing quarterbacks. “… Even at the age of 31 with a history of injury, Joey Bosa can still be a force. He tallied five sacks, nine tackles for a loss, 16 quarterback hits and a league-leading five forced fumbles in 15 games with the Buffalo Bills last year and could be a key rotational piece for San Francisco in the back half of 2026.” ESPN’s Adam Schefter reported weeks ago that Joey Bosa was leaning toward retirement, but that doesn’t mean he can’t be tempted to play again in the right situation. Playing with his brother on a Super Bowl frontrunner where he won’t be relied on to play every down could be that perfect storm of temptation for him. away.blurb: The San Francisco 49ers will head into Sunday’s matchup against the Atlanta Falcons without two of their key receivers, as Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel have both been ruled out due to injuries. Evans is dealing with issues related to his Achilles and ribs, while Samuel is sidelined because of a hamstring problem. Despite these absences, the 49ers are entering Week 7 with an impressive 6-0 record. On a more positive note, there is encouraging news about Nick Bosa , who may return from his calf injury for the game against the Las Vegas Raiders on November 8, following the team’s bye week. His potential return would significantly bolster a defense that has managed to perform well despite facing substantial personnel losses. Cornerback Jack Jones is likely to be San Francisco’s primary trade candidate, as his limited role and affordable contract present an opportunity to recover an asset before he reaches free agency. However, his first season in San Francisco has been different. Through six games, Jones has played only 71 defensive snaps, which represents about 18 percent of the team’s total defensive plays. He has yet to start a game, with his participation mainly limited to specific packages that require additional defensive backs. Despite this limited role, Jones has recorded six tackles and three passes defended, providing occasional contributions without securing a consistent place in defensive coordinator Raheem Morris’ preferred lineups. The current cornerbacks in San Francisco have contributed significantly to this situation, as Renardo Green and Deommodore Lenoir have taken on extensive responsibilities, while Upton Stout has been developing into a valuable option in the secondary. The coaching staff has shown confidence in these players, allowing the 49ers to maintain defensive consistency even with injuries affecting other positions. Jones’ experience remains beneficial, especially when Morris needs additional coverage options against teams that spread the field, but his reduced workload raises questions about whether San Francisco is getting enough value from a veteran player who could attract interest from other teams. With his contract expiring at the end of the season, General Manager John Lynch has a limited window to explore potential trade possibilities before Jones becomes eligible for free agency again. Jones has also shown an ability to make impactful plays on the field, recording eight interceptions over his first four NFL seasons. His performance in Las Vegas was particularly impressive because he intercepted three passes during the 2024 season, returning one for a touchdown. This ability highlights his anticipation and disruptive presence in coverage, and these characteristics could be appealing to teams dealing with injuries or disappointing performances at the outside cornerback position. home.blurb: San Francisco is going into the game shorthanded with fewer than 48 players available, their undefeated record (6-0) on the line. Head coach Kyle Shanahan has ruled out a handful of stars, including their main receivers. A few others are questionable for Sunday. He's discussed the need for players to stay ready because it's likely their number is called Sunday. Wide receivers Deebo Samuel Sr. and Mike Evans have been ruled out, Shanahan said after Friday's practice. Additional players that will sit out include star defensive lineman Nick Bosa, linebacker Garret Wallow, safety Marques Sigle and linebacker Luke Gifford. Cornerbacks Siran Neal and Upton Stout are questionable for the game, as is wide receiver Christian Kirk. "That's something we talk about a lot. It's every week. I think that's the hardest thing about the NFL, just how much a game takes out of people, how much a week of preparation takes out of people and how much doing it 17 times does," Shanahan told reporters. "That's what I think is one of our strengths. I think we’ve got guys who understand how this league works. They understand what has to go into it and they know that anyone can beat you." 49ers injuries: Who's out vs. Atlanta Falcons? "It's stuff we've talked about throughout the week. Hope it doesn't get to it, and odds are it won't, but it definitely could," Shanahan said when asked if guys are ready to assume roles they don't usually play. "You're always a few injuries away from those situations and now it comes down to a couple. So, percentages go up." Shanahan says the message is to not have a letdown game. The Falcons are 2-4, but Shanahan doesn't want the 49ers to overlook them. "I think when you have situations where we've won a number of games and we've got a bye-week ahead of us, it really helps when you can turn on the film and just show them," he added. "When you turn on Atlanta's film, they know how big of a challenge this is. We've got a number of guys down. We know they do, too, but they're a team that, I know the record doesn't show it, but they're a team that should be there in the end." Last Sunday's 26-20 win over the Indianapolis Colts painted a picture of a team capable of many of the metrics Robert Saleh was supposed to hit in his first season. Better late than never right? Well, we've yet to see if Week 6 was any more than a lucky break like the last six or so Tennessee wins (over two seasons) have been. Tomorrow's battle with the 4-2 Cleveland Browns should be a great litmus test either way. Ahead of that matchup, I'm making two bold predictions for the Titans: One on offense, and one on defense. We'll begin with the unit that has been less effective through six games. Cam Ward throws first TE touchdown of season Somehow, Cam Ward hasn't thrown a single score to a tight end this season. I suppose it doesn't help that he's only thrown four in general, but looks to the TEs have been extremely limited. Starter Gunnar Helm only has nine receptions for 60 yards on the season. I am predicting that both of those things will change in Week 7. Earlier this week, Ward said TEs have "one of the hardest jobs in the NFL," before hitting on his need to connect with Helm specifically. "That's something that we want to be able to do, is get Gunnar going. He's a very reliable red zone target." Fellow TE Daniel Bellinger is also involved in the passing game, and could be in line for extended looks. But after arguably Ward's worst passing performance of the year last week, OC Brian Daboll will have to mix things up if his unit is to tick in the right direction for once. It can only go up from here for the TEs. If changes are to be made, you have to think they get more involved; and if they get more involved, Helm will be the first to benefit. Titans (nearly) replicate six-sack showing from Week 6 On the flip side of the ball, I predict that the Titans' defensive line will come close to replicating their game-winning outing from last week. Saleh's front sacked Colts QB Daniel Jones a whopping six times, with DT Jeffery Simmons forcing a fumble in a different instance. Against one of the NFL's weaker offensive lines (the Browns have let Deshuan Watson be sacked a league-high 24 times), the Titans have a path to repeat that success. I don't believe the Titans will get as many as six sacks again. Although, with the defense hot and benefiting from an advantage on paper, four or five sacks feels right. Maybe a bit bold, but that's the nature of this article, after all. Simmons had 1.5 sacks by himself in the Titans' win over the Browns last December. Look for another big game from Tennessee's leading man, to boot. Aside from their records, these two teams are oddly similar. Their defenses tend to carry them and keep games close, while their offenses tend to struggle, particularly early on in games. Cleveland is well-equipped to win those slog-style games, but will they slip up in the Music City? Here are our predictions for Week 7. Anthony Moeglin It's a Cleveland Browns party on Broadway this weekend in Nashville, Tennessee. The Browns come into this game as the favorite for the first time all season and probably the last time all season. They have a chance to get to 5-2 on the year and stay in first place. They get it done on Sunday against the Titans. Spencer German Last week was a barometer game to assess how the Browns stack up with a legitimate Super Bowl contender, even if that contender was missing it's MVP quarterback. But this week, in some ways is an even bigger test of whether or not the Browns are as good as their record says they are. Great teams beat the teams they're supposed to beat and Cleveland does just that on Sunday to improve to 5-2. Yes, it is basically a Pick 'Em heading into Sunday. Cleveland is -1.5 favorites in this one, and I see a 20-3 winner for Cleveland where the defense shuts it down, and the offense gets it going a little bit on Sunday. This one is basically a Pick 'em with the Browns being listed as favorites for the first time this season (and on the road nonetheless) by 1.5. I think that means they easily cover, with a 17-9 victory. A 300-yard day for Deshaun Watson I'm 0-6 on bold predictions this year, so let's go way out there. Deshaun Watson throws for 300 yards on Sunday for the first time in his Cleveland Browns career. It would be a monumental day down in Tennessee if this bold prediction comes true. The Browns score 7 on their opening drive Despite Todd Monken's presence as an elite offensive mind, the Browns have yet to score on an opening drive this season. They've also only scored six points in the first quarter this season. In a game featuring two struggling offenses, the one that gets off to a better start could be in the driver's seat for a win. Finally, Cleveland gets to play with a lead.

Browns Pro Bowler Lands on Injury Report as Key Contributors Return The last thing the Cleveland Browns wanted was for injuries to slow down their hot start to the 2026 campaign. And while earlier in the week, it seemed that banged-up bodies were threatening to put them into Sunday's showdown as underdogs, the team's latest report gave everyone a sigh of relief. On Saturday, Oct. 24, the Browns released an update on injuries, with corresponding moves made ahead of a Week 7 meeting with the Tennessee Titans on the road in Nashville. The Browns officially activated running back Dylan Sampson off the injured list. The second-year speedster has missed the last five straight weeks due to a lower-body injury he suffered in the Browns' season opener in Jacksonville. He was injured on a kickoff. Across the last two campaigns, Sampson has played in 16 games, recording just 175 rushing yards on 65 attempts. However, he makes his impact known in the receiving game, where he took 33 receptions for 271 yards and two scores. Being dumped down in the flats from time to time, Sampson can make defenders miss with his speed. He did it with then-rookie Shedeur Sanders last season. If he gets involved in the game plan on Sunday, it will be intriguing to see how the Browns use him, especially with Quinshon also back from injury. In hopes of keeping the defensive line deep through a few injuries, the front office elevated defensive tackle Sam Kamara. Over the last two weeks, he has been a nuisance for opposing teams, recording eight total tackles, three for a loss, one sack and one quarterback hit. Finally, the Browns have placed offensive guard Teven Jenkins on the injured reserve list. He hasn't played all season, having injured his back ahead of the Browns' Week 1 opener in Jacksonville. In his place, rookie Austin Barber has thrived , being listed as one of the league's top rookies through the first few weeks of the season. To avoid Jenkins rushing back and re-injuring himself, Cleveland made the right move to shut him down through the back half of the season. Safety Grant Delpit was in concussion protocol for most of the week. But thankfully, it seems one of the Browns' most important defensive leaders will be good to play this weekend. His six-year career in the Orange and Brown has been exceptional, with him recording 476 tackles and two 100-tackle seasons along the way. He has also added eight interceptions, 7.5 sacks, 26 tackles for a loss, 24 pass deflections and three forced fumbles. A dynamic safety, Delpit's clearance is great for a Titans passing attack that is going to look to get Tony Pollard and Cam Ward going early. home.headline: Four out, four questionable for week 7 road trip against the Tennessee Titans
home.blurb: The Cleveland Browns travel to the Music City to face the Tennessee Titans at Nissan Stadium in Week 7 at 1:00 p.m. ET on CBS. After a full week of practice, the team has ruled four players out, while four players are listed as questionable to play. Defensive tackle Kalia Davis and quarterback Dillon Gabriel, who had their 21-day practice window opened in early October, have been ruled out. A decision on the rest of their season will need to come in the next couple of days. If the players are not activated, they would be lost to the reserve/injured list for the rest of the season. After missing the Week 6 home victory against the Baltimore Ravens, with running backs Jaleel McLaughlin and Audric Estime stepping in and stepping up, Judkins returns to his starting role in Week 7. He was a limited participant in practice Wednesday and Thursday, before taking part in a full practice on Friday. He was removed from the injury report when the official designations were revealed. The Browns continue to waste a roster spot, as offensive guard Teven Jenkins (back) did not practice again this week, and he has been ruled out. He hasn’t played at any point this season after suffering a back injury in practice on the Wednesday leading up to the Week 1 road trip to face the Jacksonville Jaguars. Running Back Quinshon Judkins is Back for Week 7 Judkins will get to work against a Tennessee Titans rushing defense which allows just 3.8 yards per carry, although they’re 24th in the NFL with 735 yards allowed on the ground. Tennessee has given up six rushing touchdowns, too. In addition, rookie wide receivers Denzel Boston (foot) and KC Concepcion (calf, quadriceps) were each able to take part in their first full practice of the week on Friday, and both players were removed from the injury report, too. So, quarterback Deshaun Watson will have his top two receivers at his disposal, as well as his top running back. That’s good news for an offense which can use all the help it can get. Offensive Line Gets Good News for Sunday, too Starting offensive tackle Tytus Howard (knee) and starting center Elgton Jenkins (knee) were each able to take part in a full practice on Friday, and they’ll be good to go against the Titans on Sunday.

home.headline: What Robert Saleh said about Jordan Elliott situation, response from Titans and NFL
home.blurb: "The (defensive line) room is really close," Saleh said. "For JFM to go out there and kind of help Jordan through with whatever he was dealing with at that moment I thought was really admirable on JFM’s part." The incident, which is under review by the NFL, followed a practice altercation with teammate JC Latham. Teammate John Franklin-Myers was credited with de-escalating the situation before it worsened. Tennessee Titans coach Robert Saleh confirmed on Oct. 21 that Jordan Elliott pulled a gun in the team facility's parking lot after a practice altercation last week, leading to the defensive tackle's release this week. An NFL spokesperson told The Tennessean on Oct. 21 that the Titans "promptly" notified the league about the matter, and it is under review. Saleh praised the organization and the NFL's response to the incident, citing a "pause" by the team and the league in getting Elliott assistance for what Saleh called a sign for "a cry for help" instead of involving law enforcement. "And the reason why I think the NFL and the organization did an outstanding job is because this is a man who is father, a great husband. He’s never committed a crime in his entire life," Saleh said. "And he pulled a gun in the parking lot. And the first question that I think everyone forgets to ask is why would a great man, a great father, a man who shows up on time every day, works his ass off every day, contributes the way he's supposed to contribute, is well-liked in the locker room — Why did he go off the rails and grab a gun? "And to me, those are small signs of a cry of help. In terms of, obviously there’s something greater happening. And I thought the team and the NFL did an outstanding job with regards to pausing and asking those questions and checking every single box with regards to getting him the help that he needs." Saleh vouched for Elliott's character despite the incident. The veteran defensive tackle with seven seasons in the NFL played for Saleh in San Francisco last year before joining the Titans in free agency in the spring. "These kids go through a lot. A lot. And... I will stand on the table for Jordan’s character," Saleh said. "Unfortunately, rules are rules with regards to guns on property. And sometimes it’s far greater than the knee-jerk reaction of kicking somebody when they are down. "My message to 31 other teams would be if you need a helluva run-stopping defensive tackle that can help you on a playoff run, give me a call. I’ll tell you everything you need to know about him. He’s a good man. Had a terrible lapse in judgement that I recognize as a call for help more than a criminal act." What happened with Jordan Elliott at the Titans' facility? Elliott attempted to retrieve a gun from his vehicle after a practice altercation with JC Latham on Oct. 15, according to multiple reports. picks.headline: 3 Bold Vikings Predictions as Kyle Murray & Co. Host the Colts in Week 7
picks.source: Minnesota Vikings On SI on MSN
picks.blurb: The Vikings will host a game at U.S. Bank Stadium on Sunday for just the third time this season as they welcome the 2-4 Colts to the Twin Cities in Week 7 . Minnesota looks to remain undefeated coming off an early Week 6 bye, while Indy will be scratching to salvage a start that has already led to the firing of general manager Chris Ballard . Needless to say, these are two teams currently heading in completely different directions. With a beast of a November schedule looming, here are my predictions for a Vikings team looking to put together a dominating performance. 1. Kyler Murray will rack up 300-plus yards between the air and ground While the early bye provided desperately needed injury relief for the Vikings, there are fair concerns that the break may have disrupted the progress Kyler Murray and the passing game were starting to make. Murray’s performance in New Orleans was especially promising, mainly due to the fact that the offense entered the game without wideout Jordan Addison and left tackle Christian Darrisaw, and then lost tight end T.J. Hockenson to a concussion early. With all three looking to return this weekend, I see Murray having his best day yet in purple. Indy’s 351.2 yards allowed per game rank ninth in the league, and Murray’s abilities through the air and on the ground make him especially hard to stop (h/t: Ian Hartitz). After totaling 280 total yards against the Saints (229 passing, 51 rushing), I predict Murray will finish with over 300 total yards on Sunday. 2. Vikings' offense explodes for over 30 points The Vikings’ season started with a bang, scoring 39 points in the season opener against the Packers. Since then, they have not scored more than 23 points in a game. Sunday is the perfect opportunity for that to change. The Colts have given up 27.3 points per game so far this season, the sixth-highest average in the league. Minnesota, meanwhile, is looking for its first truly dominant offensive showing as it prepares for the hardest stretch of its schedule. The returns of Hockenson and Addison should open up passing options, and Jordan Mason’s possible return to the backfield could elevate a run game that Aaron Jones has carried almost entirely on his own so far. The Vikings’ offense needs to prove it can score consistently before facing some of the league's toughest opponents, and the Colts’ shaky defense may give them plenty of opportunities. 3. Harrison Smith wakes up and snags his 40th career interception Franchise legend Harrison Smith has had a relatively quiet start to his 15th NFL season . Smith announced his return a week before the Vikings kicked off their 2026 campaign and has mostly been a rotational piece in defensive coordinator Brian Flores’s ever-evolving defense. Even though “The Hitman” is clearly past his prime, he’s still one of the smartest defenders in the game, and I expect that to pay off this weekend. Smith recently confirmed to Richard Sherman that this will be his last season , so there is no better time to snag his 40th interception than now (h/t: "Richard Sherman Podcast"). Colts quarterback Daniel Jones has thrown six interceptions this season, tied for the third-most in the league , and anyone who's watched him through his career knows he’ll eventually throw a duck or two (h/t: NFL). Smith’s football IQ and Jones’s occasional recklessness may just be the perfect combination to get the NFL’s active interception leader his next pick. Our friends from the FanDuel Sportsbook have opened the betting lines for Week 7 in the NFL, and the Vikings are starting the week as a 5.5-point favorite over the Colts. away.headline: Colts key playmaker remains sidelined with injury
away.blurb: The Indianapolis Colts are coming off their second-straight and fourth total loss of the 2026 season, and it’s safe to say a large reason why is because they were without one of their top playmakers. Unfortunately, his return to the field remains unknown. The Colts selected Warren with the No. 14 overall pick in the 2025 NFL Draft out of Penn State, where he won the John Mackey Award as the nation’s top tight end in 2024. Related Articles Bears React to NFL Announcement for QB Caleb Williams Following His Return According to Myles Simmons of Pro Football Talk, Colts second-year tight end Tyler Warren was still sidelined on Wednesday with a groin injury. It’s certainly not the news Colts fans were hoping to hear as the team is schedule to take on the undefeated Minnesota Vikings in Week 7. However, head coach Shane Steichen did provide a bit of a promising update after practice. “He’s progressing really well, but I’ll defer to the injury report this week on a lot of those guys,” Steichen said . It can’t be understated how much Warren means to the Colts’ offense. Despite missing Week 6, he still leads the team with 30 catches to go along with 213 yards and two touchdowns. In the meantime, the Colts will have to continue relying on veteran wide receivers Josh Downs, Keenan Allen and Laquon Treadwell as well as backup tight end Mo Alie-Cox. It didn’t take Warren long to establish himself as one of the best up-and-coming tight ends in the league, either. As a rookie, Warren racked up 76 catches for 817 yards and four touchdowns. The Indianapolis Colts today elevated cornerback Kenneth Harris and linebacker Germaine Pratt to the active roster from the practice squad for Sunday's game against the Minnesota Vikings. The team also released punter Thomas Morstead from the practice squad. Harris , 6-0, 192 pounds, was elevated in Week 1 vs. Baltimore and registered one solo tackle. He was signed to the team's practice squad on August 31, 2026. Harris participated in training camp with the Colts after originally signing with the team as a free agent on August 26, 2026. He previously participated in the New England Patriots' 2026 offseason program and training camp. Harris was originally signed by the Patriots as an undrafted free agent on May 8, 2026. Collegiately, he played in 59 career games (29 starts) at Oklahoma State (2023-25) and Arkansas State (2020-22) and compiled 113 tackles (92 solo), 61.5 tackles for loss, 1.0 sack, 28 passes defensed and three interceptions. Pratt , 6-3, 250 pounds, was signed to the team's practice squad on October 13, 2026. He has started 104-of-112 career games in his time with the Colts (2025-26), Las Vegas Raiders (2025) and Cincinnati Bengals (2019-24) and has totaled 734 tackles (416 solo), 38.0 tackles for loss, 3.5 sacks, 33 passes defensed, eight interceptions, eight forced fumbles, seven fumble recoveries and eight special teams stops. Pratt has started seven postseason contests and has compiled 49 tackles (32 solo), 1.0 tackle for loss, four passes defensed and one interception. In 2025, he started 12 games with Indianapolis and registered 101 tackles (57 solo), 5.0 tackles for loss, eight passes defensed, one interception, one forced fumble and two fumble recoveries. Pratt began last season with the Raiders, where he started four games and recorded 25 tackles (10 solo), 1.0 tackle for loss and two passes defensed. Morstead , 6-4, 225 pounds, was signed to the team's practice squad on October 20, 2026. He has played in 272 career games in his time with the Colts (2026), San Francisco 49ers (2025), New York Jets (2023-24, 2021), Miami Dolphins (2022), Atlanta Falcons (2021) and New Orleans Saints (2009-20). home.headline: Almost entirely good news on Vikings' first injury report of Week 7
home.blurb: Everyone on the Vikings’ active roster was at the team’s Wednesday practice. Only three players were deemed limited participants: WR Justin Jefferson (ankle), RT Brian O’Neill (knee), and CB James Pierre (foot). Typically, being a limited participant on Wednesday isn’t a major cause for concern. O’Neill and Jefferson were both questionable going into the Saints game but were able to play, which suggests they should be fine this week as well. Pierre, the Vikings’ No. 3 cornerback is a new addition to the injury report. Jefferson’s ankle might not quite be 100 percent yet, but it would be surprising if he missed this game after coming out of the Saints game without any issues. “It’s good,” Jefferson said on Wednesday. “Still taking it day by day and trying to get it feeling better and better every single day. Still wake up with those aches and pains like everybody does. But still being able to come out here, practice, get on my feet and run through it, it definitely feels good.” The Vikings are missing a couple key guys on injured reserve in Donovan Jackson and Josh Oliver, who are both likely out for the season. Outside of that, they seem to be getting healthy at a good time. After this week’s Colts game — which certainly can’t be overlooked — the schedule is going to get quite a bit more daunting, so they’ll need all of their guys available. As we’ve expected, dating back to the aftermath of the Vikings’ Week 5 win over the Saints, a well-timed bye week helped bring some positive news on Minnesota’s first injury report of Week 7. Running back Jordan Mason (thumb), wide receiver Jordan Addison (hamstring), tight end T.J. Hockenson (concussion), and left tackle Christian Darrisaw (concussion) all missed the win in New Orleans. home.blurb: LP = Limited participant in practice. DNP = Did not participate in practice. Probable = the league defines a Probable injury designation as a 75% or greater chance of playing. Historically, 95% of players designated probable are active and played on game day. Questionable = the league defines a Questionable injury designation as being 'uncertain' of whether the player will play or not. This replaces the former definition of having a 50% chance of playing. Historically, 70-75% of players with a Questionable injury designation were active and played on game day. Doubtful = The league defines a Doubtful injury designation to mean the player is unlikely to participate in the game. In practical terms, teams use the designation when a player has less than a 50% chance to suit up, and active game appearances from this designation remain rare. Historically only around 6% of players with a Doubtful designation are active and played on game day. Out = will not play. Players with this designation are not active on game day and league rules prohibit them from playing. For the Colts, they have seven starters who did not practice Wednesday due to injury. They include linebacker Bryce Boettcher, cornerback Sauce Gardner, right guard Matt Gonglaves, punter Rigoberto Sanchez, right tackle Jalen Travis, slot cornerback Justin Walley, and tight end Tyler Warren. Not much else is known at this point, but his not practicing and Sauce Gardner already likely out on Sunday could leave the Colts' struggling secondary pretty thin at cornerback.
