Both teams are looking to keep their seasons from going completely off the rails, so let’s make some predictions for this Week 7 matchup. THREE BOLD PREDICTIONS Malik Washington Sets a Season High in Receiving Yards Sunday will mark the return of rookie receiver Caleb Douglas, who has missed the past three games with an ankle injury. Adding his size to the top of the depth chart should bump everyone else to a more natural position, and there may be no bigger benefactor than Malik Washington. Washington has quietly put together an impressive third season, tallying 50 or more scrimmage yards in four of his first five games. He has also established himself as a favorite target of quarterback Malik Willis, who has thrown his way 36 times this year (more than double the second-place mark). As Miami looks for sustainability, targeting Washington underneath seems like a potential solution, and he has the agility to make defenders miss in space. His ascension, Douglas’ return, and Willis likely needing quick answers against a Jets defense that ranks eighth in blitz percentage is a recipe for a big day for Miami’s most experienced receiver. Both Quarterbacks are Sacked 3+ Times This matchup features two passers who have done a poor job mitigating pressure this season. Both rank top 12 in time to throw, top three in pressure rate allowed, and top five in sack percentage. The Jets are well equipped to take advantage of Malik Willis’ indecision. Their defense ranks in the top eight in pressure rate, and is tied for sixth in total sacks through six weeks. The Dolphins, on the other hand, have been inept up front. Their four sacks are half the next-lowest team in the NFL, and all four came against Kyler Murray and the Minnesota Vikings in Week 4. With two weeks to prepare, a quarterback who is willing to hang in the pocket, and the potentially dumb luck that Miami’s sacks have come in a bunch, this feels like a perfect opportunity for the Dolphins’ defensive front to make its mark, even if Malik Willis’ play leads to a similar outcome on the opposite side of the ball. Ollie Gordon Makes a Game-Changing Explosive Run Ollie Gordon's development in year two has been a revelation. His footwork looks substantially better than it did in 2025, and he’s made the most of his elevated opportunity. Gordon’s rushing yards over expected per attempt is ninth among qualified rushers, per NextGenStats. The Jets have a very sound defense on a per-run basis. Their EPA per rush allowed is tied for third best in football, and they’re right around the middle of the pack in terms of yards-per-attempt. They have, however, struggled to stop runs in the backfield. Their stuffed run rate is seventh-lowest, and they’re allowing over a yard and a half before contact per carry, which ranks ninth-worst. Miami’s massive offensive line has opened up big lanes for Gordon in recent weeks. He has a 20+ yard carry in each of the last two games. Now, against a defense that particularly struggles to generate displacement, it wouldn’t be shocking to see the left-side duo of Paul and Proctor give Gordon a runway that he can use to get downhill and put his massive frame to work against New York’s defensive backs. away.headline: Dolphins' Jeff Hafley returns to New Jersey seeking first Miami win
away.blurb: Coach Jeff Hafley hopes to get his first NFL head-coaching win in his home state of New Jersey. Players have identified key areas for improvement, including reducing turnovers and penalties. MIAMI GARDENS ― Miami Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley likes to say it's about the team and not about him, but he sure would like to have his first NFL head-coaching win take place in his home state of New Jersey. "My mom will be there," Hafley said of a Week 7 game at the New York Jets . "I'll have a lot of people there. My brother, my sister, I'll probably have 30-plus people at the game. For all of us, I think it's always nice to go back close to home." Hafley hails from Montvale, N.J., only 17 miles from MetLife Stadium where Sunday's game will be played. The Dolphins are 0-5 but entered the week only 4.5-point underdogs at the Jets , who are 2-4. Miami's first five opponents were NFL playoff contenders. The Jets likely are not. And here is more good news: the Dolphins are coming off of an early bye week. "New energy, man," said Dolphins linebacker Jordyn Brooks. "Just a chance to reset. away.headline: Caleb Douglas could return to Miami Dolphins lineup against New York Jets
away.blurb: “Caleb will be limited [in practice] today. You know, we’ll see how he looks today and progress to Wednesday, but I think there’s optimism there. Let’s see how it goes today, and if he can get ramped up on Wednesday, it would be good to get him back out there.” The Miami Dolphins had a much needed bye week this past weekend. Multiple players have been banged up, including standout rookie receiver Caleb Douglas. It seems the added rest has been a good thing for the young pass catcher, as according to head coach Jeff Hafley, Douglas has a chance to suit up against the New York Jets on the road this upcoming Sunday. During his press availability on Monday morning, head coach Jeff Hafley was asked about Douglas’ potential to practice this week. Hafley, with a smile on his face, would go on to speak about what Miami missed on offense without Douglas in the mix. “Just kind of looking back through the last couple of weeks, some of the things that he did, we’ve missed him. And to see a rookie kind of have to start and stop like that, not ideal. But, he’s worked really hard and it would be very great to get him back.” We will keep a close eye on Douglas’ practice participation as the week unfolds, but as of Monday afternoon, his availability seems to be pointing in a positive direction in regards to playing this Sunday.

Mayfield missed the past three games with a dislocated right thumb, but returned to practice this week wearing a protective white glove designed to add support to the area. He said Thursday the thumb has “gotten to a place where it’s strong enough to be able to play.” “It feels fine gripping it and throwing it,” Mayfield said. “It’s just the impact stuff. That was my concern. But it’s been great so far.” Buccaneers coach Todd Bowles said a day earlier that Mayfield was trending in the right direction and that he was encouraged to see his quarterback “do the things we wanted him to do.” Panthers coach Dave Canales is familiar with Mayfield’s toughness, and certainly knows how important he is to the Buccaneers (1-5). Canales served as Tampa Bay’s offensive coordinator and play-caller in 2023 and is credited with helping revive Mayfield’s career. Mayfield threw for 4,044 yards that season with 28 touchdown passes as the Bucs won the NFC South. That’s normally not a good thing for Carolina. Mayfield has dominated the Panthers in the past. He’s 6-1 against his former team as a starter, with five of those wins coming since signing with the Buccaneers. Panthers’ Bryce Young to make 50th start The Buccaneers won four straight NFC South titles from 2021-24, but have struggled since in losing 12 of their past 15 games. Carolina (3-2), which dethroned Tampa Bay as division champions last season despite a losing record, seems to be trending in the opposition direction behind a steadily improving Bryce Young at quarterback. He leads the NFL in yards passing per game. away.headline: Buccaneers Week 7 injury report: Mayfield returns, Egbuka sidelined
away.blurb: The Tampa Bay Buccaneers received encouraging news Wednesday as Baker Mayfield returned to full participation in practice after missing three games with a right thumb injury. However, wide receiver Emeka Egbuka was among five players who did not practice as Tampa Bay prepares for Sunday's NFC South matchup against the Carolina Panthers . Luke Goedeke (calf), Bucky Irving (illness), Zyon McCollum (illness) and Christian Rozeboom (finger) also missed practice. Antoine Winfield Jr. was limited with a rib injury, while Sean Tucker and Cody Mauch participated fully. Carolina quarterback Bryce Young fully participated despite a knee injury, while running back Chuba Hubbard was held out for rest. Practice designations: FP = Full Participation; LP = Limited Participation; DNP = Did Not Participate. away.headline: Buccaneers at Panthers: Thursday injury report for Week 7
away.blurb: Mayfield, who has missed the last three games after dislocating his right thumb in Week 3, continues to make progress toward a potential return. The veteran quarterback was a full participant Wednesday and Thursday, providing optimism that he could be back under center when Tampa Bay travels to Carolina. Elsewhere on the injury report, running back Bucky Irving (illness) and cornerback Zyon McCollum (illness) were upgraded to limited participation after sitting out Wednesday. Defensive tackle Calijah Kancey (illness) also improved to full participation. However, wide receiver Emeka Egbuka (concussion/foot), offensive tackle Luke Goedeke (calf), and linebacker Christian Rozeboom (finger) remained sidelined for a second consecutive day. Wide receiver Chris Godwin Jr. was also held out for rest. For Carolina, outside linebackers Jaelan Phillips (hamstring) and Thomas Incoom (calf) remained out of practice Thursday. Running back Chuba Hubbard, linebacker Devin Lloyd, offensive tackle Taylor Moton, and tight end Darren Waller all returned as full participants after receiving rest Wednesday. away.blurb: Three Pittsburgh Steelers have been ruled out for the team's Week 6 game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday, and five more are questionable to suit up, according to the team's Friday injury report. Two wide receivers Ben Skowronek and Roman Wilson left the team's 34-22 Week 5 win over the Indianapolis Colts with injures and did not return — and they won't be back this week, either. Skowronek suffered a calf injury early in the second quarter, and then Wilson injured his left hand on the final offensive drive of the first half. Wilson had a large wrap on his left hand after the game. On Monday, head coach Mike McCarthy said neither player will return to active this week. Fellow wide receiver DK Metcalf was initially listed as questionable to play after missing practice on Friday with an illness, but he has now been cleared to play. Tight end Pat Freiermuth is also questionable to play after suffering a calf injury in practice on Saturday. Strong safety DeShon Elliott remains limited in practice and will not return this week. Starting cornerback Jamel Dean was ruled out last week, but might be ahead of the curve on the initial multi-week estimate for his injury. He is listed as questionable. Running back Rico Dowdle , who is recovering from a dislocated toe on his left foot, is also questionable to make his return to the lineup, as is defensive tackle Keeanu Benton , who has an ankle injury, and defensive who has an ankle injury, and defensive back Jalen Ramsey , who has played through his broken wrist the last two weeks. A beat up Steelers defensive kept Tom Brady out of the end zone for 55 minutes and Mitch Trubisky successfully replaced an injury Kenny Pickett as Pittsburgh beat the Buccaneers, 20-18 at Acrisure Stadium on Oct. 16, 2022. Pickett threw his first career touchdown pass to Najee Harris in the first quarter, but a hit from blitzing linebacker Devin White knocked him out of the game. Chris Boswell kicked two field goals and Trubisky found Chase Claypool for a six-yard touchdown in the fourth quarter to extend the Steelers lead. With 4:45 to play, Brady finally punched through a defense that was playing without T.J. Watt , Minkah Fitzpatrick , Ahkello Witherspoon , Levi Wallace and Cam Sutton with a touchdown pass to Leonard Fournette, but Devin Bush broke up the two-point conversion attempt, and Trubisky and the Pittsburgh offense ran out the clock. Defensive run game coordinator and outside linebackers coach Larry Foote had two stints with the Steelers, playing from 2002-08 and 2010-13 after the team made him a fifth-round draft pick out of Michigan. Foote was a two-time Super Bowl champion in Pittsburgh and also won a Super Bowl LV ring as a coach with Tampa in 2021. home.headline: Jaelan Phillips is out, but his injury isn’t the only puzzle Panthers have to solve
home.blurb: Canales soon clarified that Phillips will be out for Sunday’s game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers: “I know there are advantages to game plans, but this is something that we need to address and take care of.” With Phillips officially out — it’s unclear if he’ll be ready by the Panthers’ Thursday Night Football game against the Packers in Week 8 — the Panthers are missing more than a run-of-the-mill defensive starter. The 27-year-old who the Panthers signed to a four-year, $120 million contract this free agency has lived up to his billing as a premier pass rusher; he has 2.5 sacks through five games but has also added 18 total pressures in the pass rush — 24th among all edge rushers , according to Pro Football Focus. Phillips has also been stout against the run and a vocal leader his teammates praise. What’s also a result of Phillips being out? The absence of Phillips comes at the same time as reserve outside linebacker and special teams ace Thomas Incoom is also “week to week” with a calf injury. Incoom exited the Eagles in the first half and didn’t return, and as a result the Panthers needed to do a whole bunch of roster magic to fill his role on special teams. In each of the four special teams units Incoom contributes on — kick return, kick coverage, punt return, punt coverage — the Panthers needed to replace him with four different players, Canales said. Canales was asked if the Panthers will elevate anyone from the practice squad with Phillips and Incoom out, and he indicated that Nick Hampton would. The interior offensive lineman was placed on the team’s injured reserve before the season began due to a hamstring injury and is now waiting for his 21-day practice window to be activated. When asked Wednesday, Canales was vague about Christensen’s situation: “We’re just evaluating it, and you gotta figure out roster spots as well,” before adding that he has faith in the team’s current slate of IOLs. If Christensen were to return, that limits their flexibility to use the injured reserve. It’s also worth noting the Panthers have already waived someone off the injured reserve with an injury settlement — Claudin Cherelus a few weeks ago — to avoid further limitations. It’s possible, perhaps likely, that once Cherelus gets healthy, he’d re-sign with the Panthers, rejoining the squad without forcing the team to use one of its eight precious IR-elevation moves. home.headline: Bucs elevate LB from practice squad for Week 7 vs. Panthers
home.blurb: Fordham will fill in for Rozeboom as the team’s fourth linebacker. Where he will most likely have the biggest impact is on special teams. Rozeboom has been a part of the Bucs core special teams unit, logging 27 snaps on punt coverage, 25 on kick return, 23 on punt return, seven on kick coverage and two on the field goal block unit. In total, Rozeboom’s 84 total special teams snaps rank 10th on the team. His three special teams tackles are tied for sixth-most on the team with tight ends Bauer Sharp and Ko Kieft and fellow linebacker SirVocea Dennis. Fordham is a rookie undrafted free agent out of North Carolina State. The team signed him May 9th, 2026, two weeks after the 2026 NFL Draft. Over five seasons with the Wolfpack he tallied 252 combined tackles, 18.0 for a loss, 4.5 sacks, 1 forced fumble, 2 fumbles recovered, six passes defensed and two interceptions. His 2025 campaign was his best by far as he had 143 tackles, 10 for a loss, 3.5 sacks and both of his career interceptions. The calculus surrounding the team’s roster decisions as it pertains to the 48 players who get a gameday hat change from the past few weeks. With quarterback Baker Mayfield officially questionable on the team’s injury report and all but guaranteed to play, Tampa Bay didn’t need to elevate practice squad quarterback Easton Stick. That helps them avoid a roster crunch issue as Stick was out of elevations and they would have had to add him to the roster or opt to elevate fellow practice squad passer Brett Rypien. But two new starters on the offensive side of the ball join safety Antoine Winfield Jr. as ruled out for the game on Sunday. Wide receiver Emeka Egbuka, Tampa Bays leader in targets, receptions and receiving yards will miss the game with a concussion and foot injury. The team activated receiver David Sills III off of injured reserve as the corresponding move when they placed Rozeboom on injured reserve. Right tackle Luke Goedeke has a calf injury that will keep him out of the game. Ahead of their Week 7 matchup against their divisional rival Carolina Panthers, the 1-5 Bucs are elevating just one player from their practice squad to their gameday roster, the team announced Saturday. After placing backup linebacker Christian Rozeboom on injured reserve earlier this week due to a finger injury. It makes sense that their practice squad elevation this week would lean towards that position. The team could have elevated two players but opted for only one in Week 7. This isn’t Fordham’s first elevation this year. He was previously elevated and played in Week 4, where he played four snaps on special teams himself without earning a single production stat. He played extensively during the preseason this year, logging four tackles on special teams over three games and 29 snaps. He also tallied 10 tackles and five defensive stops over 12 attempts while adding a pressure over 100 defensive snaps. Ravens HC Jesse Minter said Lamar Jackson did get in some “limited” work today. https://t.co/3rq60qmJVB The Ravens opened as three-point favorites at home in this massive Week 7 matchup against AFC North foe, and that line bounced around from 2.5 to 3 in the lead up to Wednesday's practice. However, Jackson was not spotted at the beginning of practice and was later seen walking off with a limp. As a result, oddsmakers at DraftKings quickly shifted the odds in this game to Bengals -1.5, a huge 4.5-point flip from where they were entering the week. Lamar Jackson (ankle) seen walking off practice field with a limp, per @CordellWoodland . https://t.co/1R708hsFHo That's a sign that Jackson isn't expected to play in Week 7, and he may need to log a full practice on Thursday or Friday to shift the sentiment in the betting market. Sports Illustrated spoke to multiple oddsmakers this week about how they set the line for a game like this with Jackson's status up in the air. "Your lookahead line, you essentially have to assume he's going to play until you hear otherwise.," Ty Gour, Sports Trader at Fanatics Sportsbook, told Sports Illustrated. "So, that's baked into the price, whether we anticipate he'll be at full strength or 80% strength, that would kind of be factored in there. "And then, as the week goes on, we'll adjust as we know more. Obviously, he wasn't at practice today, and our line went down a point and a half just off that alone. And then we'll kind of trickle down as the week goes on and his status becomes more and more certain one way or the other. If he's back at practice tomorrow in a limited or full capacity, the line will probably shift back towards the Ravens. If he's not there again on Thursday, we'll essentially start pricing as though [Tyler] Huntley is going to be the starter." So, what could the line close at if Huntley makes his third start in a row? "If he's out and it's Huntley again, the line will most likely shift to the Bengals being the favorite, probably in that 1.5 to 2.5 range," Gour said. So, based on Gour's projection, the current line suggest that Jackson won't play. That would be a huge blow to a Ravens team that is 4-2 and already lost a division game in Week 6. In his four games this season, Jackson completed 70.8 percent of his passes for 967 yards, six scores and just one interception. He also has 19 carries for 144 yards and a score while leading the NFL in yards per attempt, yards per completion and passer rating. The Ravens are 7-12 all time without Jackson, though they've won three of the four starts Huntley has made in his place since the 2025 season. picks.blurb: Bengals at Ravens Final Score Predictions: Experts see another extremely close AFC North battle - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football UCF stuns No. 2 BYU for its first-ever win over Top 5 team TRENDING College football updates Valkyries even WNBA Finals Kimi Antonelli on US GP pole NFL injury updates Brewers take Game 1 Thomas Shea-Imagn Images / Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Brandon Little, John Sheeran, Rob Gregson Fri, October 23, 2026 at 10:00 AM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The preseason projected winner and runner up of the AFC North face off in NFL Week 7 as the Cincinnati Bengals (3-2) take on the Baltimore Ravens (4-2). Our AFC North beat writers certainly see a barnburner when looking at their predictions. Expectations were high for both of these divisional foes, but bumps in the road have been faced on both sidelines of this rivalry. Cincinnati is trying to prove its legitimacy as a Super Bowl contender and defeat a winning team. The Ravens are dealing with familiar problems under a new coaching staff, but formidable talent is still spread across the roster. Such is the case for both rosters, really. CBS' lead broadcast crew is calling this game for a reason . It should be a close contest akin to the majority of meetings these teams have had this decade. Our AFC North beat writers certainly see a barnburner when looking at their predictions. Bengals 30, Ravens 27 The big question entering the week was whether or not the Ravens will have quarterback Lamar Jackson for this AFC North battle. After practicing each of the last two days , it's looking like he'll play. Dropping to 4-3 on the season and 0-2 in divisional play would be a rough start for Baltimore, and this game against the Bengals is one they badly need. Baltimore struggled badly on offense against the Browns after the first few drives of the game, and Week 7 will be another tough test against a good Bengals' defensive front. Cincinnati is well rested off an early bye week, and the road team in this matchup is in a similar situation: trying not to start 0-2 in AFC North play. The thing is, I believe the Bengals have an easier home to climb out of if they drop this game. With that being said, I have to roll with the Bengals coming out of the bye week. Baltimore looks like a lesser product on the field aside from Jackson at quarterback, and Burrow will have success finding his weapons against their defense. These games are always close; this one will be too. – Brandon Little, A to Z Cleveland Baltimore Ravens vs. Cincinnati Bengals History This is the 61st regular season meeting between the two franchises, and 62nd overall. Baltimore leads the all-time series, 33-28. Cincinnati won the lone playoff meeting, 24-17, during the 2022-23 NFL postseason. Lamar Jackson is 6-2 against Joe Burrow when both quarterbacks started and played the entire game. Ravens 26, Bengals 24 This is a game Bengals fans should be genuinely excited to watch. If championship aspirations are to be taken seriously, a road game against the biggest adversary in the division is an environment in which the moment is met. That doesn't mean victory is certain. The margin for error against knowledgable rival players is extremely small, but that's not an excuse to not at least look the part. Cincinnati should play well in this game. If the opposite becomes true, then it will say a lot more about where things actually stand with both the roster and coaching staff. Ultimately, I think the Ravens have a better chance of winning when it comes to the details. Derrick Henry hasn't always been efficient this year, but he's built to attack the current weaknesses of the Bengals defense. Jackson's track record against multiple iterations of the unit is solid. Baltimore may have a systemic issue blowing leads, but is Cincinnati's offense ready to finish games against a quality team? Something may give there. That's a long way to say this should be as close as it gets. Because it's likely Jackson out there and not Tyler Huntley, I'll predict the home team comes out on top. – John Sheeran, A to Z Cincinnati Assuming Jackson is back for the Ravens, this game becomes one of the best on the Sunday slate. The Bengals were off last week, while the Ravens fell to the Browns in a tight game in Cleveland. One would assume that if Jackson is playing in that game, the Ravens escape the Dawg Pound with a win. But now they face the potential of dropping two straight. The problem for Baltimore isn't just that they are playing a good Bengals team; they are playing a team off a bye, where they will be rested and prepared. We have seen some crazy battles between Burrow and Jackson over the years, and I believe we could be in for another shootout, but the Bengals offense will prove to be overwhelming for a Ravens defense that has largely been inconsistent on the back end. Give me Cincy. – Rob Gregson, A to Z Pittsburgh Final Prediction for Bengals at Steelers Two out of three predictions go the Bengals' way. Last year's series ended in a 1-1 split for the first time since the 2022 season. No one would be surprised if this year ends the same. It starts with one team landing the first blow. Unless it's a tie, in which case literally no one wins. This article was originally published on A to Z Sports. home.headline: Lamar Jackson Out for Ravens vs. Bengals, Latest Updates on QB's Ankle Injury
home.blurb: Baltimore Ravens star quarterback Lamar Jackson has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Cincinnati Bengals, the team announced Saturday. Jackson was previously listed as questionable heading into Baltimore's Week 7 matchup due to a a high ankle sprain. He was a limited participant in practice on Wednesday, Thursday and Friday ahead of the AFC North clash. "Right now, I'm headed in the right direction," Jackson told reporters Friday. "I can't call it right now, still got a grace period. We'll see, man, hopefully. But I feel like I'm heading in the right direction right now." He initially suffered the ankle sprain during Baltimore's 24-18 win over the Tennessee Titans in Week 4. The Ravens have turned to backup quarterback Tyler Huntley in Jackson's absence, and will do so again Sunday. Huntley led the Ravens to a 30-23 overtime win against the Atlanta Falcons in Week 5 before falling to the Cleveland Browns in Week 6.

home.headline: Lamar Jackson injury update: Ravens QB to miss third straight game against Bengals in Week 7
home.blurb: Lamar Jackson ruled out vs Bengals However, Baltimore will once again be without star quarterback Lamar Jackson, who has been ruled out of the matchup because of an ankle injury. "QB Lamar Jackson (ankle) has been downgraded to “out” for tomorrow’s game vs. Cincinnati," the team announced on Saturday, Although the quarterback participated in limited practice sessions this week, the team confirmed on Saturday that he would not be available against Cincinnati. Jackson’s return to the practice field offered some encouragement, but the Ravens remained cautious about declaring him fully fit for Sunday’s game. The 29-year-old was listed as “questionable” on Friday’s injury report, with Minter suggesting that his availability could be decided shortly before kickoff. However, the Ravens ultimately made the decision earlier. Jackson details key return factor The Ravens quarterback also clarified that managing the pain would be more important than the reduction in swelling when assessing his readiness to return to action. The Baltimore Ravens will face the Cincinnati Bengals on Sunday in Week 7 of the NFL season as they look to recover from last week’s defeat to the Cleveland Browns. The Ravens split their last two games against the Atlanta Falcons and Cleveland Browns without Jackson. Ravens cautious about Jackson’s recovery "He's been able to get some work in these past couple of days," Ravens coach Jesse Minter confirmed on Friday. "Between Lamar and our staff, it's going to be a decision based on him and how he feels and how effective it could be. He's had a good couple of days, but we'll see how it goes over the next 48 hours,” the coach had mentioned. Jackson was sidelined from practice for two weeks after suffering the injury in Week 4. However, he provided an optimistic update on Friday, telling reporters that his recovery was “headed in the right direction.” "I feel like the swelling went down a lot. It's just the pain tolerance. Just trying to move how I move. If I can't do that, I can't help my team,” he said. Ravens’ starting QB in Jackson’s absence With Jackson sidelined again, Tyler Huntley is expected to take over as Baltimore’s starting quarterback. Huntley would start his third game of the season in place of the injured Jackson, continuing his role as Baltimore’s temporary starting quarterback. He has performed reliably in relief, avoiding interceptions across three appearances and posting a 1-1 record in his two previous starts.

home.headline: Baltimore Ravens rule out Lamar Jackson for third consecutive game
home.blurb: The Baltimore Ravens will head into their Week 7 NFL clash against the Cincinnati Bengals without starting quarterback Lamar Jackson. The team confirmed on Saturday that Jackson has been downgraded to out, marking the third consecutive game he will miss due to an ongoing ankle injury. Despite participating in limited practice sessions throughout the week, the organization ultimately determined that the 29-year-old is not yet ready for game action. The decision follows a period of uncertainty regarding his status, with the team previously listing him as questionable on Friday’s injury report. Speaking to reporters on Friday, Jackson expressed optimism about his progress, noting that while the swelling in his ankle has significantly subsided, his primary concern remains pain management. The quarterback emphasized that his ability to move naturally on the field is the critical factor in determining his return, stating that he cannot effectively assist his team if he is unable to perform his usual movements. The Ravens enter the Sunday matchup looking to rebound following a loss to the Cleveland Browns last week. The team has split their last two games during the period Jackson has been unavailable, and they will look to Huntley to lead the offense as they face the Bengals in a pivotal mid-season contest. Ravens coach Jesse Minter had previously indicated that the decision regarding Jackson’s availability would depend on the player's physical comfort and his ability to perform at an effective level. While Jackson returned to the practice field this week after a two-week absence, the team maintained a cautious approach to his rehabilitation. With Jackson sidelined, Tyler Huntley is set to step into the starting role for the third time this season. Huntley has served as the primary replacement during Jackson’s absence, maintaining a 1-1 record in his previous two starts. Throughout his three appearances this year, Huntley has managed to avoid throwing any interceptions, providing a steady presence for the Baltimore offense. home.headline: Ravens Week 7 injury report vs. Bengals: Lamar Jackson’s status puts Baltimore offense in limbo again
home.blurb: The Baltimore Ravens enter Week 7 against the Cincinnati Bengals with their biggest offensive question still unanswered. Lamar Jackson is questionable with an ankle injury after participating on a limited basis in all three practices, leaving Baltimore to prepare without certainty at quarterback. Jackson’s practice involvement keeps a return possible, but the report offers no confirmation that he will play. His availability remains the central storyline for an offense that must account for both his passing ability and the pressure his mobility puts on opposing defenses. Baltimore’s official player page documents Jackson’s ankle injury and his recent progression back to limited practice. That provides context for his participation, but it does not settle his availability against Cincinnati. Lamar Jackson’s questionable status leaves Baltimore balancing two plans Jackson’s Wednesday, Thursday and Friday designations followed an identical pattern: limited participation. There was no listed setback, but there was also no upgrade to full participation before the final injury report. Rashod Bateman progressed from limited participation Wednesday to full sessions Thursday and Friday while managing a shoulder injury. Matthew Hibner followed that same progression with a hand issue. Baltimore also received encouraging participation from several offensive linemen. Guards Olaivavega Ioane, John Simpson and Andrew Vorhees each moved from limited work Wednesday to full participation over the final two practices. None received a game designation. Ronnie Stanley’s week requires a more careful reading. Listed with rest, toe and ankle concerns, he went from limited Wednesday to full Thursday before missing Friday. However, he has no game designation. Baltimore has already ruled out safety Jaylinn Hawkins and outside linebacker Tavius Robinson. Hawkins missed the final two practices with a knee injury, while Robinson did not practice all week because of a pectoral injury. Cornerback T.J. Tampa is doubtful after three limited practices with a knee issue. Defensive lineman Broderick Washington is questionable following the same participation pattern because of an ankle injury. The defensive absences could narrow Baltimore’s options for rotations and substitutions. Combined with Jackson’s uncertain availability, they leave the Ravens facing important personnel decisions on both sides of the ball before kickoff against a divisional opponent, with limited margin for further disruption. Houston, now at 2-4 but having won two straight road games against division rivals, returns to NRG Stadium to host the New York Giants of New Jersey. The Giants, sitting at 3-2-1, come into this matchup atop the NFC East, despite not winning in their last two games, a tie at Washington and a loss against New Orleans. They have only beaten the Giants once in 6 total meetings, and that was in 2002. Sandwiched between an international game and a bye week, this has the feel of a trap game for Houston. This particular line may tighten a bit as the week progresses, especially as the Giants sort out their QB situation and both teams sort out their respective injury situations. away.headline: Giants Activate Paulson Adebo, Place Tremaine Edmunds on IR Ahead of Texans Game
away.blurb: Adebo, who was placed on IR at the start of the season with a knee injury, will get the start at cornerback with Greg Newsome II (concussion) declared out this week. The Giants downgraded two players who originally had questionable designations, tight end Theo Johnson (neck) and safety Jevon Holland (concussion). Johnson did not make the trip with the team to Houston. Holland is believed to have traveled with the team, but it doesn't matter as he's been declared out for Sunday. New York also elevated safety Raheem Layne from the practice squad to give them added depth what with Tyler Nubin (neck) having a questionable designation and Holland having been downgraded to out. Tremaine Edmunds Reportedly Out for Season as Giants Finalize Injury Statuses for Week 7 The New York Giants ’ roster churn continued Saturday as the team activated cornerback Paulson Adebo from injured reserve. It placed inside linebacker Tremaine Edmunds on IR with a season-ending shoulder injury. “He’s a legit corner. He’s a cover corner, he tackles. He’s been a high-end corner in this league. I think he’s really determined to play that way,” head coach John Harbaugh said of Adebo and what the cornerback can bring to the defense. “I think he’s finally probably healthy and ready to go. I can’t wait to see it.” Adebo is in the middle of a three-year, $54 million contract with the Giants that included $38.5 million guaranteed and $34.75 million fully guaranteed. However, he lost his starting job this summer to Deonte Banks, who, along with Newsome, has been the starting cornerback tandem for the Giants. Two Giants ' Statuses Downgraded for Sunday In other roster news, receiver Jalin Hyatt, who has been sitting on the team’s practice squad this season, is one of two standard practice squad elevations this week. Hyatt was the team’s third-round pick in 2023. He has appeared in 41 games with 10 starts over three seasons and has 36 receptions for 470 yards and no touchdowns. The Giants have only been carrying four receivers of late and last week they nearly lost one when Darnell Mooney suffered an injury that cut into his playing time. New York Giants' Shocking Injury News Just Changed Everything - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL UCF stuns No. 2 BYU for its first-ever win over Top 5 team TRENDING College football updates New York Giants' Shocking Injury News Just Changed Everything (Sam Navarro-Imagn Images) Matthew Schmidt Sat, October 24, 2026 at 11:00 AM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads As if the New York Giants didn't already have enough injuries, they just lost yet another key players for the year, as linebacker Tremaine Edmunds has gone down with a season-ending shoulder injury. Edmunds popped up on the injury report this week with the shoulder issue, but it didn't appear to be too big of a deal. Evidently, it was more serious than initially anticipated. Now, the Giants have lost the anchor of their linebacking corps, the man they signed to a three-year, $36 million contract in free agency back in March. New York's run defense was already struggling as it was, so to subtract Edmunds on top of that will make things that much more challenging for Big Blue. Micah McFadden will now step back into a starting role, and fortunately, he has long proven to be serviceable — but he is a definitive downgrade from Edmunds. This injury changes absolutely everything for the Giants. Edmunds' absence will now put that much more pressure on rookie Arvell Reese, and it also means that Reese's mentor will no longer be on the field with him. Reese has looked spectacular in certain moments this year, but he has also looked very much like a first-year player at other times, so losing Edmunds will unquestionably have an effect on the youngster. And of course, it will also give running backs yet even more of a chance to break through the Giants' linebacking corps and into the defensive backfield. New York has now lost two of its top defensive players in Edmunds and Brian Burns, which is beyond devastating for a unit that displayed so much potential during the season opener. The Giants are now incredibly thin on that side of the ball, and in an NFC East that is totally up for grabs, New York may slowly be losing its advantage. To make matters worse, the schedule is about to get tougher. The Giants will face the suddenly hot Houston Texans on the road on Sunday before heading into their bye week. Then, New York will begin a difficult stretch that runs all the way through Week 18. Even in such a horrendous division, it's becoming harder and harder to view the Giants as a potential playoff team given all of their injuries. First, Jaxson Dart . Then Burns. Now Edmunds. It continues to snowball.

In the Chicago Bears 30-24 win over the New England Patriots , they triumphed despite allowing one of the most unique "Hail Mary" touchdown passes in recent memory. Patriots quarterback Drake Maye's 48-yard checkdown touchdown pass to running back Rhamondre Stevenson was the only touchdown pass in the last 20 years in the final 10 seconds of a half, 40-plus yards from the end zone on a throw of 10 or fewer air yards, per CBS Sports Research. What other craziness could happen during the rest of the NFL's Week 7 lineup? Daniel Jones cuts through Brian Flores' No. 1 Vikings defense The Minnesota Vikings are 5-0, and it is very much on the strength of defensive coordinator Brian Flores' aggressive unit. They are an immovable object. Flores' defense leads the NFL in: Scoring defense (12.8 points per game allowed) Third down defense (22.2% third down conversion rate allowed) Red zone defense (27.3% red zone touchdown rate allowed) Goal-to-go defense (33.3% goal-to-go touchdown rate allowed) Completion percentage allowed (53.2%) Touchdown-to-interception ratio allowed (3-6) Sack rate (9.8%) Pressure rate (46.4%) Blitz rate (69.8%) The Vikings' blitz rate of just under 70% (69.8%) is the highest by any team in any five-game span in the last 10 seasons, per CBS Sports Research. So how is that going to go for Indianapolis Colts quarterback Daniel Jones in Week 7? Well, the bold prediction here is that he doesn't commit any turnovers and totals multiple touchdowns against Flores' unit. Jones' splits versus the blitz are the exact same in terms of yards per pass attempt this season (5.9), and he actually has a higher completion percentage, touchdown-to-interception ratio, and passer rating against the blitz in 2026. Jones also got to spend the second half of the 2024 season watching how Flores' unit operates up close in practice on a daily basis after Minnesota scooped him up for depth purposes after his New York Giants release. That practice experience against Flores will allow Jones to produce a clean, efficient performance. Daniel Jones vs. the blitz, 2026 season Pass attempts Completion percentage Pass yards per attempt Air yards per attempt Passer rating Bijan Robinson goes runs wild vs. the undefeated 49ers The undefeated San Francisco 49ers not only have a top-five scoring offense (29.5 points per game) but also a top-10 scoring defense (18.3 points allowed per game). That also extends to their run defense, which ranks as the seventh-best in football, allowing just 90.2 rushing yards per game. Bijan Robinson , who enters Week 7 leading the NFL with 785 yards from scrimmage, will go off for 150-plus rushing yards against San Francisco. He'll be well rested after having just 11 touches in Week 6, his fewest in a game since 2024, and Robinson will break what has been one of the 49ers' biggest strengths: their control of outside-zone runs. San Francisco has curbed outside-zone runs to just 3.2 yards per carry, the sixth-fewest in the NFL, and they are the only defense that hasn't allowed a gain of 10 or more yards on those runs, per the NFL's Next Gen Stats. They have also tackled rushers for a loss or no gain on 5 of 29 outside-zone carries, 17.2%. Robinson has 10 explosive runs (gains of 10 or more yards) on his 65 outside-zone carries, tied with Derrick Henry for the most in the league. He's also only been stuffed for no gain or a loss on 6 of his 65 outside-zone run carries. Robinson will repeatedly cook the 49ers, rushing to the outside, and he'll become not only the first player with over 100 yards rushing against San Francisco in 2026 but the first player to hit at least 150 yards rushing against San Francisco. Cardinals stun Broncos without scoring a touchdown The Arizona Cardinals (2-4) upset the preseason Super Bowl favorite Los Angeles Rams 18-16 in Week 6 as 13.5-point road underdogs, earning the second-largest upset win by any team in the last five seasons, according to CBS Sports Research. They accomplished that feat despite not finding the end zone one time. Arizona's 18 points came from six made field goals. The Cardinals host the Denver Broncos (4-2) while seeking their first win away from SoFi Stadium -- both of Arizona's wins have come on the road against the Rams and the Los Angeles Chargers . Denver enters Week 7 with a top 10 scoring defense (20.8 points per game, 10th in the NFL), but Arizona will upset them too for their first home win of the season. Even more impressively, the Cardinals will also beat the Broncos without scoring a touchdown, just like they did with the Rams in Week 6. How will that work? Arizona will pull off that near-impossibility thanks to the Broncos' offensive ceiling being capped by starting quarterback Bo Nix . Nix's 5.6 yards per pass attempt are the fewest in the NFL among quarterbacks to start every game in 2026, and his 4.9 air yards per pass attempt represent the shortest average pass length through six games in the last 20 seasons, according to CBS Sports Research. Not having to defend the deep ball will allow the Cardinals to get creatively aggressive on defense, and Nix will give Arizona's similarly shaky offense, led by journeyman Jacoby Brissett, enough latitude to win with six or seven made field goals and no touchdowns. J.J. McCarthy avoids being sacked vs. Will Anderson Jr., Texans The New York Giants have a new starting quarterback for Week 7 at the Houston Texans : Minnesota Vikings' 2024 10th overall pick castoff J.J. McCarthy . He ranked dead last in the NFL in completion percentage (57.6%), touchdown-to-interception ratio (11-12) and passer rating (72.6) among 33 qualified quarterbacks in 2025. He also had a 10% sack rate last season, the third highest in the entire league. However, McCarthy will not be sacked in his debut as the Giants' starting quarterback despite facing the Houston Texans and All-Pro edge rusher Will Anderson Jr. , the NFL's sacks leader with 7.5 entering Week 7. How will that happen? Perhaps McCarthy has taken a big leap from 2025 to 2026. After checking in for a benched Jameis Winston in the fourth quarter in Week 6, McCarthy threw for 243 yards, the most by any quarterback in the play-by-play era (since 1991) who had no passing yards in the first three quarters, per CBS Sports Research. The humbling he took, being traded for a 2027 fifth-round pick, plus playing in a more simplistic offense in New York under offensive coordinator Matt Nagy and senior offensive assistant Greg Roman, will allow McCarthy to play a cleaner game in Week 7. That will help him avoid Anderson Jr. and Danielle Hunter's clutches as he avoids being sacked all game long. Dolphins take a lead for the first time this season The Miami Dolphins ' 2026 season is going exactly as one would expect for a franchise paying more for players not on its roster (an NFL-record $179 million in dead cap hits) than for the players on its roster ($156 million). They're 0-5 and have the NFL's worst scoring offense, averaging 14 points per game. They're also just the second team in the Super Bowl era (since 1966) to not have a lead in the first five games of a season, along with the 2005 Houston Texans, per CBS Sports Research. However, they will acquire their first lead in a game of the 2026 season against the New York Jets . The Jets have the worst red zone offense (37.5%) in the NFL, and they haven't scored a touchdown on their last seven red zone trips, which spans the last three games. New York has also been outscored 100-6 in the final two minutes of the first half under Aaron Glenn. Miami will capitalize on Glenn's end-of-the-first-half mismanagement and take a lead in a game for the first time this season. Nix has been a shell of himself through six weeks in the 2026 season, yet Denver is somehow 4-2 and favored on the road against the Arizona Cardinals in Week 7. Arizona is coming off a massive upset win on the road against the Los Angeles Rams, and while it may not be a playoff team, the Cardinals are not a pushover this season. Jacoby Brissett and Co. will have their work cut out for them against a Denver defense that is one of the best in the NFL. The Bronco offense (29th in success rate) hasn’t been able to get much going during this 4-2 start, but the defense has forced 10 turnovers and is allowing just 5.0 yards per play. The play on that side of the ball has stayed intact even with Pat Surtain II (missed the last two games) and Talanoa Hufanga (missed Week 6) injured. Arizona’s defense is one of the weaker ones that the Broncos have on the schedule, so Sean Payton may look to get his young quarterback going early on Sunday. Will it lead to a Denver win? All season long, the SI Betting team is sharing final score predictions for every NFL game, and we’re hoping it’ll help our readers decide on some spread, moneyline and total bets along the way. Plus, who doesn’t want to get an exact score bet right during the season? Denver is favored on the road, but can bettors trust this offense with Nix struggling? This spread suggests we could see a close game, so let’s dive right into my score prediction for this Week 7 battle. Broncos vs. Cardinals Score Prediction This week, SI Betting’s Iain MacMillan continued his quest to bet on every NFL game in his Road to 272 column . In this matchup, he’s taking Denver to win and cover despite some early struggles on offense: You can throw all of the Broncos' middling metrics out the window, because no team has had a tougher schedule to begin the season than Denver. They've faced the Chiefs, Jaguars, Rams, 49ers, Chargers, and Seahawks, and came out on the other end of that run with a 4-2 record. Despite playing that good a record, their defense still ranks sixth in opponent EPA per play and fifth in opponent success rate. Just imagine how good this defense is going to look when facing lower-tier competition. The Cardinals may be coming off the upset of the year over the Los Angeles Rams, but they enter this week ranking dead last in the NFL in net yards per play at -1.4. Their offense is solid at times, but their defense remains one of the worst units in the league. Give me the Broncos as road favorites. MacMillan has confidence in the Broncos this week, but I’m eyeing the UNDER with the Denver offense looking like one of the worst in the NFL. Arizona’s offense has been able to move the ball with Brissett under center, but Denver has been an elite defense the last few weeks, moving up into the top-12 in the league in points allowed, yards per play allowed, EPA/Play and success rate. The Cardinals are ninth in success rate and 15th in EPA/Play on offense, yet they’ve still scored 21 or fewer points in three of their six games. I expect Brissett to have a much tougher time against a Denver pass defense that – without Pat Surtain II – dominated Seattle and Los Angeles in back-to-back weeks. On the other side of the ball, how can anyone bet on Denver to put up points? The UNDER has hit in five of the Broncos’ six games this season, partially due to the fact that they’ve scored 23 or fewer points in five games and 20 or fewer points in four games. away.headline: Broncos place OLB Jonah Elliss on injured reserve
away.source: USA TODAY Touchdown Wire on MSN
away.blurb: The Denver Broncos have placed outside linebacker Jonah Elliss ( ankle ) on injured reserve, ruling him out for at least the next four games. “He’s going to be someone that it’s not season-ending, and so we’re fortunate," Payton said on Wednesday. "So that’ll come out later in the week, but it was better news.” Elliss will miss games against the Arizona Cardinals, Kansas City Chiefs, Carolina Panthers and Las Vegas Raiders before being eligible to return against the Pittsburgh Steelers in Week 12 (Denver has a bye in Week 10). The news is not a surprise after Elliss was spotted at a college football game wearing a walking boot and using crutches last weekend. Shortly thereafter, he wrote "Be right back 🤙🏽" on social media alongside ‭‭James‬ ‭1‬:‭2‬-‭4, a Bible passage about remaining joyful during trials that test faith and produce steadfastness. Broncos coach Sean Payton indicated earlier this week that the pass rusher's ankle injury is not-season ending. To fill Elliss' former spot on the 53-man roster, the Broncos activated fellow outside linebacker Jonathon Cooper, who is now back on the active roster after being reinstated by the NFL. away.headline: Latest Broncos' injury report indicates key players are nearing a return
away.blurb: Running back Jonah Coleman, who has been designated to return from IR with his ankle injury, practiced in full on Wednesday. Patrick Surtain II, who left the team's Week 4 game with an ankle injury, was also at practice on a limited basis: Unfortunately, Tyler Badie, Talanoa Hufanga, and Jonah Elliss all did not practice, and Elliss' injury could end up being more extended. Hufanga hurt his ankle in Week 5 against the Los Angeles Chargers, and both Badie and Elliss got hurt in Week 6 against the Seattle Seahawks. Fortunately, Hufanga's injury is minor. As for Surtain, James Palmer is reporting that the likely return for the Defensive Player of the Year is Week 8 against Kansas City, but he also didn't totally shut the door on Surtain playing this week : Him practicing in limited fashion does give him a chance to play, but you almost want to wonder if the Broncos understand the opponents they have coming up and want to ease Surtain back into things for Week 8, as that game could carry major impact across the division and conference in terms of seeding. All in all, the Broncos seem to be trending toward being more 'full strength' for the Chiefs game in Week 8. However, not only could Coleman find his way back into the lineup in Week 7, but, until he's ruled out, Surtain could be nearing a return as well. The Broncos also have wide receiver Pat Bryant on IR. He is eligible to return f in Week 9 against the Carolina Panthers. Denver plays Arizona, Kansas City, and Carolina before the Week 10 bye, which just so happens to line up nicely with the trade deadline. This article was originally published on predominantlyorange.com as Latest Broncos' injury report indicates key players are nearing a return . The Denver Broncos have dealt with their share of injuries this year, unfortunately. The bright side though, is that the Broncos are consistently among the least-injured teams in the NFL, and the ailments this year have largely been minor. As the middle of the season approaches, the playoff race will slowly start to heat up, and Week 8 against the Kansas City Chiefs could present a legitimate playoff atmosphere. Before the Chiefs, though, the Broncos have to get by the Arizona Cardinals in Week 7. And in the team's first injury report of the week, it does seem to indicate that the team could get some key players back. away.headline: Cardinals get troubling Jeremiyah Love injury update before Broncos game
away.blurb: Arizona held Love out of last week’s matchup against the Los Angeles Rams, giving the rookie additional time to recover from his ankle injury. For Love, the priority remains getting healthy enough to return without risking another setback. While Arizona has not officially ruled him out for Sunday, the latest report suggests the team may need to prepare for another game without one of its most important young offensive players. Giants DC Threatens Players Amid 'Unacceptable' Behavior, Calls Out 'Traitors' The Arizona Cardinals could be without one of their most promising offensive weapons for another week. Rookie running back Jeremiyah Love is expected to miss Sunday’s matchup against the Denver Broncos as he continues recovering from an ankle injury, according to CBS Sports’ Matt Zenitz. Love already missed Arizona ‘s Week 6 victory over the Los Angeles Rams, and the latest report suggests the Cardinals could be forced to play without their starting running back for a second consecutive game. The former Notre Dame standout did not participate in Wednesday’s practice, raising further concerns about his availability heading into Week 7. Love has been dealing with an ankle injury that initially surfaced following Arizona’s Week 4 matchup against the New York Giants. Although he returned to action against the Detroit Lions in Week 5, the rookie struggled to find his rhythm, finishing with just 22 rushing yards on 12 carries. Before being sidelined, Love had rushed for 245 yards and one touchdown on 67 carries through five games. He also contributed 11 receptions for 36 yards and another touchdown. Arizona selected Love with the third overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, making him the highest-drafted running back since Saquon Barkley went second overall in 2018. The Cardinals entered the season with high expectations for the former Fighting Irish star, who established himself as one of college football’s most explosive offensive players. Now, his early NFL career has been interrupted by injuries. With Love expected to remain sidelined, Arizona could once again turn to Tyler Allgeier and Bam Knight to handle the rushing responsibilities. The Cardinals leaned on their running back depth during last week’s victory, but facing Denver presents another challenge for an offense attempting to establish consistency. The Cardinals have invested heavily in the rookie’s long-term future, and his availability will be an important storyline as the season progresses. Love already missed Arizona ‘s Week 6 victory over the Los Angeles Rams, and the latest report suggests the Cardinals could be forced to play without their starting running back for a second consecutive game. The former Notre Dame standout did not participate in Wednesday’s practice, raising further concerns about his availability heading into Week 7. Love has been dealing with an ankle injury that initially surfaced following Arizona’s Week 4 matchup against the New York Giants. Although he returned to action against the Detroit Lions in Week 5, the rookie struggled to find his rhythm, finishing with just 22 rushing yards on 12 carries. Before being sidelined, Love had rushed for 245 yards and one touchdown on 67 carries through five games. He also contributed 11 receptions for 36 yards and another touchdown. Arizona selected Love with the third overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, making him the highest-drafted running back since Saquon Barkley went second overall in 2018. The Cardinals entered the season with high expectations for the former Fighting Irish star, who established himself as one of college football’s most explosive offensive players. Now, his early NFL career has been interrupted by injuries. With Love expected to remain sidelined, Arizona could once again turn to Tyler Allgeier and Bam Knight to handle the rushing responsibilities. The Cardinals leaned on their running back depth during last week’s victory, but facing Denver presents another challenge for an offense attempting to establish consistency. The Cardinals have invested heavily in the rookie’s long-term future, and his availability will be an important storyline as the season progresses. Most recently, the Matt LaFleur-led squad dispatched of the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday Night Football, 23-13. It marked the third consecutive game in which Green Bay held its opponent to 14 or fewer points. And on the season, the Packers’ defense – coordinated by former Arizona Cardinals head coach Jonathan Gannon – has allowed the 10th-fewest points in the NFL (20.8/game). Meanwhile, on the opposite side of the ball, Green Bay – led under center by sixth-year passer Jordan Love – has scored the 10th-fewest points in the game (21.2/game). Through six weeks, Love has also completed just 59.7 percent of his pass attempts. If the season ended today, it'd rank as his lowest completion percentage as a starting quarterback in the NFL. Yet, multiple Green Bay pass-catchers have flourished, most notably wide receivers Christian Watson and Matthew Golden. Watson, now in his fifth NFL season, has already amassed as many touchdowns as last season (six) and nearly as many receptions (29) and reception yards as he did a year ago (538). The former second-round pick secured 35 catches and 611 yards in 10 games a season ago. Meanwhile, Golden, Green Bay's first-round pick in 2025, has already surpassed all his receiving totals from his rookie campaign. He's already racked up 30 catches, 501 yards and three touchdowns amid a career breakout season. And just like Watson, he's well on pace for a 1,000-yard receiving campaign. Consequently, both Watson and Golden possess the potential to wreak havoc against the Lions’ secondary, even with Pro Bowl safety Brian Branch back in the fold for Detroit. In addition to Watson and Golden, the Lions will also likely have their hands full with Packers running back Josh Jacobs. The Pro Bowler returns to the lineup after spending the first six weeks of the season on the commissioner exempt list for an offseason domestic abuse incident. Jacobs, who's coming off a 929-yard, 13-touchdown rushing campaign in 2025, should provide an immediate boost to Green Bay's league-worst ground game. In case you were wondering, the Packers have compiled a measly 359 total rushing yards through the season's first six games. Expect Jacobs, along with Watson and Golden, to give Kelvin Sheppard's defense its fair share of fits on Sunday. away.headline: Jordan Love's inclusion on Week 7 injury report unnerves Packers heading into a crucial visit to Detroit
away.blurb: Some of the usual suspects made their weekly appearances on the Green Bay Packers' injury report heading into a Week 7 matchup with the Detroit Lions, but the inclusion of quarterback Jordan Love was a bit of a shocker for fans and journalists alike. Love was listed as a limited participant on Wednesday due to back issues, which is a new problem for him in his young NFL career. With all that said, a limited practice on a Wednesday shouldn't be too much of a cause for concern, as that's a typical veteran rest day, and one where teams often try to take it easy on their highest-leverage players. It's just surprising to see Love, who's generally so healthy and eager to practice, pop up on the injury report in the middle of the week. Although the return of Josh Jacobs should help with that to some degree , Green Bay's run blocking has been abysmal to start the season, and they'll continue to lean heavily on Love's arm to get the job done against a horrid Lions secondary. Josh Jacobs has clear role to fill in questionable Packers return Packers OC's comments on Josh Jacobs' return paint a worrisome picture for the offense Love himself does not seem concerned, as the Packers' star quarterback told ESPN's Rob Demovsky , there's "no chance" he misses Sunday's game in Detroit, but that decision isn't ultimately up to the 27-year-old quarterback. As for his head coach, Matt LaFleur told Demovsky that after the Cowboys game, Love "was pretty beat up. He took some shots. I saw him in there with the chiropractor postgame, so I knew something was up.” Jordan Love says he's okay, but Green Bay Packers fans should monitor the practice reports heading into a pivotal Week 7 visit to Detroit. Every game matters when the standings are so close, but Week 7 provides a particularly fascinating outlook given the state of the NFC North . Detroit is 3-2 on the season for the fourth spot in the division, but if they win against the Packers on Sunday, they'll leapfrog past them for either the third or fourth spot in the division. Meanwhile, if the Packers lose and the rest of the division wins, Green Bay will find itself back at the bottom of the NFC North after clawing its way back up to No. 2 in the ranking. This makes Love's status for the competition far more important than it would be in, say, Week 8 vs. Carolina, or Week 12 in New Orleans. Love is averaging a career-best 280.7 yards per contest through six weeks with 11 touchdowns to four picks, despite his completion percentage and passing success rate both dropping from last season. That's in large part due to the spike in volume we've seen in the early stretch of the season, with the Packers' run game being effectively non-existent. With that being the case, this is poised to be a huge week for Jordan Love, so long as he can stay healthy. away.headline: Green Bay Packers RB Josh Jacobs contrite as he prepares to play again amid ongoing NFL investigation
away.blurb: The NFL is still investigating Jacobs over the incident, so the league still could hand out more discipline to the three-time Pro Bowl running back. But for now, Jacobs is eligible to play again for the Packers after missing the first six games of the season. “I thought I’d be playing sooner,” Jacobs said. “But, you know, the optics of everything, I understand the other side. For me, like I said, I’m just grateful to be able to play. It was one of them things where I didn’t want to sit the whole year and then figure it out. I’m just grateful to be back on the team and to be back playing.” Today's E-Editions Chicago Tribune Advertise with Us Advertise with Us Branded Content Paid Partner Content Print (Opens in new window) Print Email a link to a friend (Opens in new window) Email GREEN BAY — Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs expressed contrition as he returned to practice Wednesday and talked with reporters for the first time since pleading no contest to two misdemeanor charges stemming from a May altercation with his then-girlfriend during which she said he threw her to the ground. “Obviously, man, I’m remorseful and sorry for putting this team in this situation,” Jacobs said. “Sometimes when you go through life, situations occur and a four-second, three-second decision can alter your life, honestly.” Jacobs was removed this week from the commissioner’s exempt list, which had prevented him from playing or practicing. The NFL had placed Jacobs on that list Aug. 30 , shortly after charges were filed against him . He pleaded no contest last month to misdemeanor counts of battery and criminal damage to property. The Packers (4-2) face the Lions on Sunday in Detroit. Jacobs was arrested May 26 , three days after police officers came to his Wisconsin home to investigate a disturbance. According to police, the woman told them that Jacobs grabbed her and threw her to the ground as she was trying to exit a garage door, causing her to hit her head. Police said Jacobs also took her phone from her while she was on the ground. Police said they noticed redness on her face and neck and could feel a bump on the back of her head. The criminal complaint against him noted that a surveillance video from the camera system in their garage corroborated the woman’s statement. Both Jacobs and the victim have gone to court attempting to have that video and other evidence sealed permanently . Jacobs declined to discuss the specifics of his case but said he hopes to use the situation as an opportunity to grow into a better person. “You never want to be in this situation, but just me being honest, for my life, it was probably one of the best things to ever happen to me,” Jacobs said. “I say that because it gave me a chance to sit down and reevaluate what’s important and what I want my life to look like, and what do I want people to know me for. away.headline: Josh Jacobs officially activated for Packers’ Week 7 game vs. Lions
away.blurb: After being on the NFL commissioner’s exempt list to begin the season, running back Josh Jacobs was finally given the green light to return. With the Green Bay Packers set to take on the Detroit Lions on Sunday, it appears he’ll actually get a chance to play in Week 7. Reports indicate that the 28-year-old ball carrier has officially been activated to join Green Bay’s roster, according to Ian Rapoport of the NFL Network. For now, it’s unclear exactly how involved Jacobs will be in the offense, but expectations are for him to receive the bulk of the workload out of the backfield. “Significant transactions: — The Packers have activated RB Josh Jacobs to the active roster from the exempt list,” Rapoport reported. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The eight-year veteran has been at the center of controversy for his alleged involvement in a domestic violence incident during the offseason. He was initially given five charges, including felony strangulation/suffocation, along with four misdemeanors. Jacobs accepted a plea deal in early September. It’s said that a judge ordered Jacobs to pay a $1,000 fine, along with costs for the battery charge and property damage charge. Those charges can be dismissed if the three-time Pro Bowler were to complete counseling, pay restitution, and avoid any contact with the alleged victim. Packers head coach Matt LaFleur has also come under fire for some of his comments about Josh Jacobs . LaFleur has openly stated he believes in second chances and that Jacobs is an individual who is currently learning from a mistake. Week 7 will be the star running back’s 2026-27 season debut. He re-joins his teammates after finishing last year with 929 rushing yards and 13 touchdowns on 234 rush attempts. Like ClutchPoints’ content? Be sure to follow us. away.blurb: Packers rule out Zaire Franklin, list four questionable vs. Lions | Week 7 Injury Report Skip to main content Primary nav News Evan Siegle, packers.com LB Zaire Franklin GREEN BAY – Packers have officially ruled out linebacker Zaire Franklin (shin) and listed four questionable for Sunday's NFC North matchup with the Detroit Lions. The four questionable are guard Aaron Banks (knee/toe), cornerback Benjamin St-Juste (hamstring), receiver Bo Melton (back) and defensive tackle Jordon Riley (Achilles), who's currently on the physically unable to perform list and would need to be added to the 53-man roster to play against the Lions. Sunday will mark only the second game Franklin has missed in nine NFL seasons, snapping a streak of 48 consecutive games played dating back to Week 8 of the 2023 season when the former All-Pro linebacker sat out against Carolina with a knee injury. The Packers could have reinforcements on the way up front against the Lions and star running back Jahmyr Gibbs, as Riley appears to be nearing a return. The third-year defensive tackle has practiced in a limited capacity the past two weeks, his first on-field work since tearing his Achilles last December. Banks has been out since injuring his toe against the New York Jets in Week 2. The 6-foot-5, 325-pound guard was also battling knee tendinitis at the time of his toe injury. Veteran Laken Tomlinson has started the past three games at left guard. The Packers didn't issue a game status for the following players who will be available: quarterback Jordan Love (back), edge rusher Lukas Van Ness (illness), cornerback Brandon Cisse (shoulder/neck), defensive tackle Anthony Campbell (ankle), and receivers Christian Watson (ankle), Matthew Golden (shoulder) and Savion Williams (ankle). Lions safety Brian Branch (Achilles) and center Cade Mays (wrist) were full participants in practice this week but are both questionable for Sunday. picks.headline: Rams vs. Raiders bold predictions for NFL Week 7
picks.blurb: Rams vs. Raiders bold predictions for NFL Week 7 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football UCF stuns No. 2 BYU for its first-ever win over Top 5 team TRENDING College football updates Valkyries even WNBA Finals Kimi Antonelli on US GP pole NFL injury updates Brewers take Game 1 Rams vs. Raiders bold predictions for NFL Week 7 Kiyoshi Mio-Imagn Images Douglas Fritz, ClutchPoints Thu, October 22, 2026 at 6:41 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads There is a big time injury for the Los Angeles Rams . And the Raiders have a major concern as well. These teams meet in Week 7, and here are bold predictions for the NFL contest. It's a crucial game for the Rams, who stand at 2-4 and find themselves a staggering four games behind the front-running 49ers in the NFC West. Meanwhile, the Raiders stand at 3-3 in third place in the AFC West. They're unlikely to be a playoff contender, but are trying to build a strong foundation for 2027. Let's take a look at what could happen when these teams battle. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Matthew Stafford will throw for three touchdowns It's hard to gauge what kind of yardage output Stafford will have. Without the injured Davante Adams, the Rams may lean on the ground game a little more. Adams is the team's leading receiver with 480 yards and four touchdowns. Sure, Stafford still has Puka Nacua. And Nacua will get his targets and yardage. But who steps into the No. 2 role? Maybe the Rams will use tight end Tyler Higbee more. Or perhaps Konata Mumpfield or Jordan Whittington will step up and produce. However, despite the receiver situation, the Rams will need to find a way to get the ball into the end zone if the Raiders load up to stop the run in the red zone. So look for Stafford to spread it around and still get his TD passes. Stafford said he understands the situation , according to The Athletic. "I just feel even more responsibility to try to be as good as I can be to help us continue to win," Stafford said. "In some of those guys' instances where they're going to have opportunities to hopefully come back and play for us, make sure that when they come back and play for us, it's meaningful stuff for them." However, some observers think Stafford has finally reached the end of his NFL rope, according to ESPN. "Stafford can't move," Ben Solak wrote. "He was never the most mobile quarterback, but the Rams were willing to use him on boots in the past. In 2024, 16.8% of Stafford's pass attempts were on the run — an above-average number! That fell to 13.9% in 2025 and is down to 9.6% in 2026. Sure, designed rollouts are down — but it isn't just that. "Stafford has zero scrambling passing yards on the season per NFL Next Gen Stats. He has yet to break the pocket and complete a pass on a scramble drill. The last quarterback to log no scramble passing yards through six weeks of a season was 2022 Tom Brady — the final season of a pocket passing titan." But it's not time to write Stafford off. Rams RB Kyren Williams will rush for 90-plus yards The Rams must run the football against the Raiders, a team that struggles to stop the ground game. The Raiders are giving up 134.3 yards per game, which ranks No. 28 in the NFL. Keeping the ball on the ground needs to be a big part of the Rams' game plan. The Rams have thrown 252 passes with 148 rushing attempts. McVay wants those numbers closer together , according to theramswire.com. "Ultimately, what I care about and what we care about is what's the best way is to move the ball and score points," McVay said. "Because of some of the situations that we've been in, those two-minute situations have gotten us a little bit out of balance. No matter how I cut it, it's an excuse. I'd like to be able to have a little bit more balance. And that's reflected by being efficient on early downs and sustaining drives." One thing is for sure, Williams and the Rams haven't lost their belief that this can be a special season. "Man, my confidence is still as high as ever," Williams said. "We know what we've got on our team and in this locker room. We come to practice every single week. That's why we can't lose our focus. We can't lose what matters the most, and that's the work. "It's about having faith. That the work we put in every single week will come to shine." Raiders RB Ashton Jeanty will split carries with Mike Washington Jr. There's no doubt that Jeanty has been a huge disappointment for the Raiders. They picked him No. 6 overall, expecting a franchise-changing player. Instead, Jeanty has a career average of 3.5 yards per carry. And Washington has been turning heads with the coaching staff, according to a post on the Raiders' YouTube page via Athlon Sports. But he needs to be better at pass protection . "He's a rookie, so he had a lot to catch up on," Kubiak said when asked about Washington's role in the passing game. "He's continuing to improve. (And) he's putting the work in. You see the practice come to life in the games. He's not where he wants to be. He's got to keep growing." Jeanty has been a threat in the passing game. Maybe his future is as a third-down back. Washington could supplant him. And the prediction is for that to begin this week. Jeanty has time to bounce back. It's still early in his career. But he simply hasn't been able to show in the NFL what he showed in college. away.blurb: On Wednesday, Trent McDuffie and Nate Landman both missed practice. Defensive tackle Tonka Hemingway was the only non-participant for the Raiders. Five other players were limited, including Brock Bowers and Kolton Miller. away.headline: NFL week 7 injury report: Raiders' Quay Walker and Rams' Puka Nacua listed
away.blurb: Las Vegas Raiders linebacker Quay Walker has been downgraded to questionable with a chest injury ahead of Sunday’s game against the Los Angeles Rams. The change raises uncertainty about his availability for the Week 7 matchup at Allegiant Stadium. ESPN’s Raiders reporter Ryan McFadden reported the downgrade on X on Saturday. Walker had been a full participant in Friday’s practice after being limited on Wednesday and Thursday, according to the Raiders’ official injury report. The injury report also lists running back Mike Washington Jr. as questionable for Las Vegas with foot and back issues. For Los Angeles, wide receiver Puka Nacua is questionable with a calf injury, while linebacker Nate Landman has been ruled out with a concussion. Walker was limited during the first two practices of the week before completing Friday’s session without a game-status designation on the team’s published report. The subsequent downgrade means his availability remains uncertain, although the available reporting does not establish whether he experienced a setback or explain the reason for the change. The Raiders host the Rams on Sunday, Oct. 25, with kickoff scheduled for 4:25 p.m. ET. Las Vegas will need to clarify Walker’s status before the game, while his questionable designation leaves open the possibility that he could still play. The late change comes as Las Vegas looks to halt a three-game losing streak. The Raiders enter the matchup at 3-3, third in the AFC West behind the Kansas City Chiefs at 5-0 and Denver Broncos at 4-2. Walker is listed as a linebacker on the Raiders’ roster. His potential absence would give Las Vegas another defensive issue to assess before facing a Rams team that enters Week 7 at 2-4, fourth in the NFC West. Los Angeles has lost its last two games, including a narrow 18-16 defeat to the Arizona Cardinals on Oct. 18.

It wouldn't make sense to give up now, especially since Garrett should come back, and Adams could return later this season as well.
