away.headline: Rams Week 7 injury report vs. Raiders: Where Davante Adams, Puka Nacua injuries leave LA offense
away.blurb: The Los Angeles Rams enter Week 7 against the Las Vegas Raiders without Davante Adams and with another major question surrounding Puka Nacua . Adams is out, while Nacua is questionable with a calf injury after missing Friday’s practice. That combination leaves Los Angeles preparing for two different offensive scenarios: building around an available Nacua or operating without either receiver. Neither offers the flexibility the Rams would have with both in the lineup. The concern extends beyond redistributing targets. Losing receiving options can change defensive coverage, third-down decisions and red-zone planning. With Adams unavailable, Nacua’s status becomes the biggest remaining variable in determining how aggressively Los Angeles can attack through the air. Nacua had no injury listing Wednesday, was limited Thursday and did not participate Friday. That progression raises concern because his involvement decreased before the final report, although it does not establish the injury’s severity or confirm he will miss kickoff. His questionable designation leaves the possibility of playing open. It does not guarantee a normal workload if he is active. The underlying objective would be keeping the offense ahead of the chains. Third-and-long becomes harder when established receiving options are unavailable and defenses can concentrate attention elsewhere. Los Angeles also has uncertainty on defense. Cornerback Trent McDuffie is questionable with a groin injury after missing all three practices. Inside linebacker Nate Landman is out with a concussion following three nonparticipation listings. For the offense, the takeaway is straightforward: Adams’ absence reduces its options, and Nacua’s availability determines how extensive the adjustment becomes. Los Angeles needs a sustainable plan for either outcome, not an assumption that questionable means ready for an unrestricted workload. The Rams list him with 37 receptions for 417 yards and one receiving touchdown across four appearances this season. If Nacua plays, Los Angeles must balance using its remaining centerpiece with whatever workload he can handle. Walker had been a full participant in Friday’s practice after being limited on Wednesday and Thursday, according to the Raiders’ official injury report. The injury report also lists running back Mike Washington Jr. as questionable for Las Vegas with foot and back issues. For Los Angeles, wide receiver Puka Nacua is questionable with a calf injury, while linebacker Nate Landman has been ruled out with a concussion. Walker was limited during the first two practices of the week before completing Friday’s session without a game-status designation on the team’s published report. The subsequent downgrade means his availability remains uncertain, although the available reporting does not establish whether he experienced a setback or explain the reason for the change. The Raiders host the Rams on Sunday, Oct. 25, with kickoff scheduled for 4:25 p.m. ET. Las Vegas will need to clarify Walker’s status before the game, while his questionable designation leaves open the possibility that he could still play. The late change comes as Las Vegas looks to halt a three-game losing streak. The Raiders enter the matchup at 3-3, third in the AFC West behind the Kansas City Chiefs at 5-0 and Denver Broncos at 4-2. Walker is listed as a linebacker on the Raiders’ roster. His potential absence would give Las Vegas another defensive issue to assess before facing a Rams team that enters Week 7 at 2-4, fourth in the NFC West. Los Angeles has lost its last two games, including a narrow 18-16 defeat to the Arizona Cardinals on Oct. 18.

home.headline: Rams Week 7 injury report vs. Raiders: Where Davante Adams, Puka Nacua injuries leave LA offense
home.blurb: The Los Angeles Rams enter Week 7 against the Las Vegas Raiders without Davante Adams and with another major question surrounding Puka Nacua . Adams is out, while Nacua is questionable with a calf injury after missing Friday’s practice. That combination leaves Los Angeles preparing for two different offensive scenarios: building around an available Nacua or operating without either receiver. Neither offers the flexibility the Rams would have with both in the lineup. The concern extends beyond redistributing targets. Losing receiving options can change defensive coverage, third-down decisions and red-zone planning. With Adams unavailable, Nacua’s status becomes the biggest remaining variable in determining how aggressively Los Angeles can attack through the air. Nacua had no injury listing Wednesday, was limited Thursday and did not participate Friday. That progression raises concern because his involvement decreased before the final report, although it does not establish the injury’s severity or confirm he will miss kickoff. His questionable designation leaves the possibility of playing open. It does not guarantee a normal workload if he is active. The underlying objective would be keeping the offense ahead of the chains. Third-and-long becomes harder when established receiving options are unavailable and defenses can concentrate attention elsewhere. Los Angeles also has uncertainty on defense. Cornerback Trent McDuffie is questionable with a groin injury after missing all three practices. Inside linebacker Nate Landman is out with a concussion following three nonparticipation listings. For the offense, the takeaway is straightforward: Adams’ absence reduces its options, and Nacua’s availability determines how extensive the adjustment becomes. Los Angeles needs a sustainable plan for either outcome, not an assumption that questionable means ready for an unrestricted workload. home.headline: NFL suspends Buffalo Bills safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson for 1 game for spitting at Las Vegas Raiders
home.blurb: After splitting the 2024 season between the Rams and Baltimore, White re-signed with the Bills and had 16 starts last season. He didn’t rule out another return to Buffalo after completing his one-year contract last season. Today's E-Editions Chicago Tribune Advertise with Us Advertise with Us Branded Content Paid Partner Content Print (Opens in new window) Print Email a link to a friend (Opens in new window) Email ORCHARD PARK, N.Y. — The NFL on Monday suspended Buffalo Bills safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson for one game without pay for spitting in the direction of Las Vegas Raiders players on the field during a game a day earlier. Gardner-Johnson was ejected late in the second quarter for unsportsmanlike conduct following an exchange with a group of Raiders players, including tight end Brock Bowers. In issuing the suspension, the league cited its rule applying to “any act which is contrary to the generally understood principles of sportsmanship.” With Buffalo (5-1) entering its bye week, Gardner-Johnson’s suspension will begin on Oct. 26 and run through Nov. 2, a day after the Bills host the Baltimore Ravens. The player has the right to appeal the suspension. Gardner-Johnson apologized to his teammates immediately following Buffalo’s 33-30 win, and has since posted a note on social media apologizing to fans. “I owe my teammates an apology and to be a man about it,” Gardner-Johnson said following the game. “You got to understand that as a grown man you can’t be doing (stuff) like that in a game,” he added. “As a vet, I’ll be better. I’ll take my consequences as it is, handle it like a man and move on.” The 28-year-old won a Super Bowl with the 2024 Philadelphia Eagles and is on his sixth team in eight seasons. Gardner-Johnson was signed by the Chicago Bears in October 2025 and appeared in 10 games with 51 total tackles. He signed a one-year contract with Buffalo in March. Coach Joe Brady referred to Gardner-Johnson’s spitting act as being “inexcusable,” and said he’s discussed the matter privately with the player. “It can’t happen. That’s not what we’re about. That’s not what the game of football is about, and he knows that,” Brady said. Gardner-Johnson arrived in Buffalo with an established reputation of being a noted trash-talker and as someone who has on occasion crossed the line with illegal hits. “I don’t need a roster of everybody being the same person,” Brady said. “Obviously, he crossed the line yesterday and that can’t happen. It won’t happen again. Personality-wise, I’m not afraid to have people who are going to try to toe the line in everything they do.” Also, the Bills are bringing back a familiar face with cornerback Tre’Davious White agreeing to sign to the team’s practice squad, a person with knowledge of discussions told The Associated Press. home.blurb: Rams Injury Report, Week 7 at Raiders: Puka Nacua and Trent McDuffie questionable, Nate Landman ruled out Skip to main content Primary nav TEAM WOODLAND HILLS, Calif. – Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua (calf) is questionable for Sunday's game against the Raiders at Allegiant Stadium in Las Vegas (1:25 p.m. PT, FOX). Nacua left Thursday's practice early with the aforementioned calf injury. Head coach Sean McVay on Friday said Nacua "took part in a majority of the practice, left, (and then) got it checked out." McVay also said that "I don't think he (Nacua) knows exactly when it occurred." Cornerback Trent McDuffie (groin) is also listed as questionable. McDuffie did not practice all week. Meanwhile, inside linebacker Nate Landman (concussion) was ruled out, but is "making good progress," McVay said. With Landman out, McVay confirmed Los Angeles will elevate inside linebacker Eric Kendricks from the practice squad. This weekend, Seattle will host the 5-0 Kansas City Chiefs on Sunday Night Football. Kansas City is coming off a frustrating 2025 campaign, which ended with a record of 6-11. That was the first time they had a losing season under Andy Reid, and they've already turned things around. Much of that is due to Kenneth Walker III, the former Seahawk who has been electric for the Chiefs . Seattle needs to find a way to contain Walker, while also figuring out how to get their ground game on track, which could happen with Zach Charbonnet set to return to action. If they can do that, they will have a chance to score the upset. As the game nears, let's see who the experts believe will walk away with the win this weekend. "The Chiefs, who’ve never fielded a top-15 rushing attack during Mahomes’ time as a starter, rank second with an average of 159.8 ground yards per game," Kownack wrote. "Walker leads the league with 665 rushing yards -- and that’s despite the fact that he’s played one fewer game than the next three leading rushers (Bijan Robinson, James Cook III and Derrick Henry), thanks to K.C.’s Week 5 bye. Meanwhile, the Seahawks have yet to finish a game with a 100-yard rusher, and their well-documented struggles on the ground are putting too much on Sam Darnold’s plate, as evidenced by the quarterback’s seven interceptions in the past four weeks." It won't be easy, and it never is when going against Patrick Mahomes. Throw in Walker and this offense is nearly impossible to stop. What gets overlooked with the Chiefs, however, is how well they've played defensively this season. CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Oct. 21 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. New England Patriots at Chicago Bears (-3) (TNF) Dajani (Bears -3): I can't remember the last time I've been this excited for a Thursday night game. Caleb Williams will suit up for the first time at home since his hamstring injury, and this is the first Bears home game since the passing of Mike Ditka. I have concerns about this Bears pass defense and how it will fare against a red-hot Drake Maye , but the fact is that Chicago has allowed 9.3 points per game at home this season. The Bears' offense has also averaged 35 points per game in their four wins, and I think Williams is out to make a statement. This will be a high-flying affair that comes down to the very end, and a push is very much in play. But give me Chicago at home, with the backing of an emotionally charged atmosphere. Remember, the Bears' lone Super Bowl win came against the New England Patriots under Ditka. … Prediction: Bears 28, Patriots 24 Dubin (Bears -3): I also see this being a high-scoring game, with two offenses that can pile up points quickly. Chicago's offense in two non-rain/non-Brian Flores games with Caleb Williams under center has been electric, particularly on the ground, and Caleb Williams opens things up for the passing game. New England is struggling to run the ball, but Drake Maye has been on fire as of late. I'll lean toward the Bears here because of the Patriots' injury issues along the offensive line, which could hold the run game back further and put even more on Maye's shoulders. … Prediction: Bears 31, Patriots 27 Pittsburgh Steelers (-3.5) vs. New Orleans Saints (Paris) Dajani (Saints +3.5): The Steelers are impossible to figure out. From week-to-week — or even half-to-half, as evidenced by last week's overtime victory against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . If you're going to give me the hook at +3.5 in an international game, I'm probably going to take it. The Saints are a perfect 8-0 ATS in their last eight games away from home, and are 3-0 ATS all-time in international games. I think Gayle Benson's recent comments stirred up the locker room, and the Saints responded with a win in which they dropped 34 points — even if it came against the New York Giants . … Prediction: Steelers 23, Saints 20 Dubin (Steelers -3.5): The Saints finally played a game from ahead last week against the Giants, and they didn't necessarily look comfortable doing it. They have mostly been a second-half offensive team throughout this season, struggling early on before piling up yards and points in comeback mode. I don't trust this offense enough to build a lead against Pittsburgh's defense (ninth in yards, 12th in points, fifth in EPA per play) right now, so I'll lean toward this game playing out in a similar fashion to New Orleans' early-season contests, with the Steelers taking a lead and the Saints trying to stage a comeback, only to fail this time around. … Prediction: Steelers 21, Saints 17 San Francisco 49ers (-3) at Atlanta Falcons Dajani (Falcons +3): I'm thinking about backing the Falcons in this spot. It looked like we were in for a blowout after the 49ers went up 23-3, but Washington then outscored San Francisco, 14-0, while outgaining the 49ers 201 yards to 7 yards. That was ... interesting to see. The 49ers have found a way to keep winning games despite all of the injuries. Nick Bosa , Mike Evans , Deebo Samuel , Upton Stout and Mykel Williams were among the players who did not practice on Wednesday. This week, I'm going to take the points with Atlanta. … Prediction: 49ers 22, Falcons 20 Dubin (49ers -3): This line feels several points too low, even with Mike Evans potentially out in addition to all of the other wide receiver issues. So long as the Niners have Kyle Shanahan calling plays and Brock Purdy , Christian McCaffrey and George Kittle involved, I think their offense cooks. And Atlanta can't quite reach the same level offensively — even with Bijan Robinson and Drake London on hand. The Niners have been excellent against the run this year, and if this game winds up being one where Penix has to match Purdy throw for throw, I don't see that going well for Atlanta. … Prediction: 49ers 26, Falcons 16 Cincinnati Bengals at Baltimore Ravens (-3) Dajani ( Bengals +3): The Bengals are fresh off their bye while the Baltimore Ravens are fresh off ... a loss to the Cleveland Browns . It was their 15th loss when leading by at least seven points in the fourth quarter since 2020, which ranks the most in the NFL. Lamar Jackson has a chance to return this week, but I'm curious to see how "spry" he looks. The two-time NFL MVP was playing some fantastic ball before the unfortunate ankle injury, and it's worth mentioning he's 7-2 in his career against Joe Burrow . I was high on the Bengals entering this season, and I'm not ready to move off that take. I think this Baltimore secondary is in for a tough test in stopping Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins . The former averages 120.4 receiving yards per game vs. the Ravens, while the latter caught two touchdowns the last time he faced them. Higgins actually hasn't faced Baltimore since Oct. 6, 2024! It's been a while. Give me the upset here. We aren't 100% sure if Jackson is even returning to the lineup, and he'll have to face one of the best interior pass rushes in the NFL. Dexter Lawrence , Jonathan Allen and Kris Jenkins Jr. are the only defensive tackle trio to record multiple sacks this season. … Prediction: Bengals 29, Ravens 27 Dubin (Ravens -3): I'm assuming that Lamar Jackson is back for this game. If he's not, then you can switch my pick to the Bengals. If Jackson is in alongside Derrick Henry and Zay Flowers , I just don't think this Baltimore offense can be stopped. When those three have shared the field this season, the Ravens are averaging 9.9 yards per play. NINE POINT NINE. Unfortunately, the sample size is only 63 plays due to injuries to Jackson and Flowers at different times. HOWEVER, I will mention that Kelvin Sheppard 's unit forced five straight three-and-outs from the Cardinals in that 45-21 win in Week 5. Plus, Brian Branch is set to return to the lineup as well. Nobody except maybe Kenneth Walker III is doing it at a higher level than Jahmyr Gibbs right now, either. Meanwhile, Green Bay can throw the ball all over the yard, and everyone throws it on the Lions. Maybe Green Bay can actually run with some efficiency in Josh Jacobs ' potential return, but it's not like he was all that efficient last season, either. So, can they turn things around on the road against a divisional opponent? The Eagles enter this game on a four-game losing streak, and star quarterback Jalen Hurts is out for the season with blood clots in his lungs. That is a massive blow to the Eagles in the futures market, as they’re now last in the odds to win the NFC East and +15000 to win the Super Bowl. Tanner McKee is set to make another start in Week 7, and this may turn into a lost season for an Eagles team that could decide to trade some veteran pieces to recoup draft capital and lighten the load on the salary cap in years to come. Oddsmakers have set the Cowboys as favorites in this matchup, and a win would put Dallas in a much better position to win the NFC East – which it is still favored to do. away.headline: Eagles will be without DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks, while Saquon Barkley is questionable vs. Cowboys
away.blurb: DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) were ruled out on the final injury report released Saturday afternoon. Smith is set to miss his third game of the season because of his lingering hamstring issue, while Wicks will miss his first. Wicks, the 25-year-old receiver, appeared to injure an ankle late in the Eagles’ loss to the Carolina Panthers . Without Wicks, the Eagles will call on Makai Lemon to step up. The first-round rookie receiver out of Southern Cal said Friday that Monday’s game will provide him with a “big opportunity.” “I’m just super excited to go out there with the guys,” Lemon said. “Put on a good performance. Had a great week of practice with all the guys. So just trying to go out there and execute. Couple guys are out, so really just next man up. I’ve got a bunch of trust in the guys next to me. Trust in the coaches and the game plan. So I’m definitely excited for this week’s matchup.” Meanwhile, running back Saquon Barkley is listed as questionable for Monday’s game after missing the last two contests with a hamstring injury. He said Thursday that he would “love” to make his return against the Cowboys. He was a full participant in Saturday’s practice. Tight end Dallas Goedert is available. He did not practice Thursday or Friday, but he returned on Saturday as a full participant. Goedert said Saturday that the knee injury he has been dealing with is the same one that sidelined him for two games earlier this season. He said he had “a little bit of inflammation in there,” but once it settled down, he felt good enough to return to practice. “Just making sure I tested out there full speed, but it felt good,” Goedert said. “For me, it’s just really letting the coaches know that I’m good and be able to be out there for whatever they need me for.” The Eagles also are banged up defensively. A pectoral strain kept him sidelined throughout training camp and the start of the season, and now the ankle injury has him in and out of the lineup. Outside linebacker Jalyx Hunt (knee/ankle) also is questionable. home.headline: Eagles will be without DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks, while Saquon Barkley is questionable vs. Cowboys
home.blurb: DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) were ruled out on the final injury report released Saturday afternoon. Smith is set to miss his third game of the season because of his lingering hamstring issue, while Wicks will miss his first. Wicks, the 25-year-old receiver, appeared to injure an ankle late in the Eagles’ loss to the Carolina Panthers . Without Wicks, the Eagles will call on Makai Lemon to step up. The first-round rookie receiver out of Southern Cal said Friday that Monday’s game will provide him with a “big opportunity.” “I’m just super excited to go out there with the guys,” Lemon said. “Put on a good performance. Had a great week of practice with all the guys. So just trying to go out there and execute. Couple guys are out, so really just next man up. I’ve got a bunch of trust in the guys next to me. Trust in the coaches and the game plan. So I’m definitely excited for this week’s matchup.” Meanwhile, running back Saquon Barkley is listed as questionable for Monday’s game after missing the last two contests with a hamstring injury. He said Thursday that he would “love” to make his return against the Cowboys. He was a full participant in Saturday’s practice. Tight end Dallas Goedert is available. He did not practice Thursday or Friday, but he returned on Saturday as a full participant. Goedert said Saturday that the knee injury he has been dealing with is the same one that sidelined him for two games earlier this season. He said he had “a little bit of inflammation in there,” but once it settled down, he felt good enough to return to practice. “Just making sure I tested out there full speed, but it felt good,” Goedert said. “For me, it’s just really letting the coaches know that I’m good and be able to be out there for whatever they need me for.” The Eagles also are banged up defensively. Edge rusher Nolan Smith (concussion) was ruled out on Saturday’s injury report. He did not practice all week. Defensive back Michael Carter II (abdomen) also was ruled out and will miss his second straight game. Jonathan Greenard (ankle) is listed as questionable. He said Saturday that he would be a game-time decision as he deals with what he described as an ankle sprain. Greenard practiced Thursday as a limited participant and did not practice Friday or Saturday, but he refuted the notion that he experienced a setback. Greenard, who signed a four-year, $100 million deal with the Eagles upon being traded from the Minnesota Vikings in April , has been active for just three games this season. A pectoral strain kept him sidelined throughout training camp and the start of the season, and now the ankle injury has him in and out of the lineup. Outside linebacker Jalyx Hunt (knee/ankle) also is questionable. Hunt, the Eagles’ 2024 third-rounder out of Houston Christian, was injured in the Week 5 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars and missed last week’s game against the Panthers. home.headline: Cowboys vs. Eagles Injury Report
home.blurb: Dallas Goedert is good to go for Monday, while Saquon Barkley and Jalyx Hunt inch closer to a potential return. "It's just kind of the same injury that I sustained earlier. I just had a little bit of inflammation in there, had to let that settle down, but felt really good running out there today," Goedert said after Saturday's practice. "I want to be out there anytime I can. We only get 17 games. To miss a game, to miss two games, it always stinks. So if I can be available, I'm going to do everything I can to play. "I'm going to go out there and do whatever I can to help the team win, whether it's run blocking, pass blocking, or hopefully get a couple catches. We're looking forward to this game playing on Monday night against the division rival. It's going to be a lot of fun. The atmosphere's going to be great and it's a game I wouldn't want to miss." Two of the Eagles' top receivers, DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle), have been ruled out, leaving rookie first-round pick Makai Lemon as the primary wide receiver option. "It's definitely a big opportunity with the team," Lemon said. "I'm just super excited to go out there with the guys, put on a good performance. Had a great week of practice with all the guys. So, just trying to go out there and execute. A couple guys are out. So really just, next man up. I got a bunch of trust in the guys next to me, trust in the coaches and the game plan." Running back Saquon Barkley (hamstring) took a step forward and was a full participant at practice on Saturday after being limited previously in the week. The running back is listed as questionable for Monday night. Meanwhile, Jonathan Greenard (ankle), who did not practice again on Saturday, is listed as questionable. The edge rusher said it will be a game-time decision as he will need to see how his ankle feels. Alongside Greenard, the outside linebacker room is banged up. Jalyx Hunt (knee/ankle) could return on Monday as he is listed as questionable after practicing in a limited capacity all week. Nolan Smith (concussion) has been officially ruled out. Smith is joined by defensive back Michael Carter II (abdomen). Cornerback Jakorian Bennett, tight end Grant Calcaterra, guard Landon Dickerson, and tight end Eli Stowers all participated fully in practice on Saturday. They are all listed as questionable since they are on Injured Reserve and would need to be activated by Monday afternoon in order to play against the Cowboys.
